questions.prompt: Show that there is no arithmetic progression with three elements in the infinite geometric sequence $\{2^k\}_{k=0}^\infty$.
questions.answer: If $2^k<2^l<2^m$ were in arithmetic progression, then $2^{l+1}=2^k+2^m$, i.e. $2^{l+1-k}=1+2^{m-k}$ — an odd number $\ge 3$ equal to a power of $2$, impossible.

questions.prompt:

$$\det\begin{pmatrix}0&a_{12}&a_{13}&\dots&a_{1n}\\-a_{12}&0&a_{23}&\dots&a_{2n}\\-a_{13}&-a_{23}&0&\dots&a_{3n}\\ \vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\-a_{1n}&-a_{2n}&-a_{3n}&\dots&0\end{pmatrix},$$
where $n$ is an odd number.

Let $[x]$ be the integer part of $x$. Find the limit
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\Big((\sqrt3+1)^n-\big[(\sqrt3+1)^n\big]\Big).$$
questions.answer: The limit does not exist

questions.prompt: Let $f(x)$ be an even, twice continuously differentiable function and $f''(0)\ne0$. Prove that there is an extremum of $f(x)$ at the point $x=0$.
questions.answer: Evenness gives $f'(0)=0$ (the one-sided difference quotients at $0$ are negatives of each other); then $f''(0)\ne0$ and the second-derivative test (Taylor with $f''$ continuous) give a strict extremum.

questions.prompt:
Find the $n$th derivative of the function
$$f(x)=\frac{x}{x^2-1}.$$
questions.answer: $f^{(n)}(x)=\dfrac{(-1)^n n!}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{(x+1)^{n+1}}+\dfrac{1}{(x-1)^{n+1}}\right)$ for $x\ne\pm1$ (partial fractions).

questions.prompt:
Prove that there exist two real convex functions $f,g$ such that
$$f(x)-g(x)=\sin x$$
for all $x\in\mathbb R$.
questions.answer: Take $f(x)=x^2+\sin x$ and $g(x)=x^2$: $f''=2-\sin x>0$ and $g''=2>0$.

questions.prompt:
Prove that for all integers $n>1$,
$$(n-1)\mid\left(n^n-n^2+n-1\right).$$
questions.answer: Modulo $n-1$ we have $n\equiv1$, so $n^n-n^2+n-1\equiv1-1+1-1=0$ (equivalently: $x=1$ is a root of $x^n-x^2+x-1$).

questions.prompt: Let $X$ be a finite set and $f\colon X\to X$ be a map. Prove that $f$ is an injective map if and only if $f$ is a surjective map.
questions.answer: With $|X|=n$: injective $\Rightarrow$ $|f(X)|=n$ $\Rightarrow$ $f(X)=X$; surjective $\Rightarrow$ the $n$ fibres $f^{-1}(y)$ are nonempty, disjoint and cover $n$ elements, so each has exactly one element.

questions.prompt:
Prove that for a continuously differentiable function $f(x)$, where $f(a)=f(b)=0$,
$$\max_{x\in[a,b]}|f'(x)|\ge\frac{1}{(b-a)^2}\int_a^b|f(x)|\,dx .$$
questions.answer: By the mean value theorem $|f(x)|=|f(x)-f(a)|\le (b-a)\max|f'|$, so $\int_a^b|f|\le(b-a)^2\max|f'|$.

questions.prompt:
Find all functions $f\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ which satisfy the equality
$$xf(y)+yf(x)=(x+y)f(x)f(y)$$
for all $x,y\in\mathbb R$.
questions.answer: $f\equiv0$, and the functions with $f(x)=1$ for all $x\ne0$ and $f(0)=a$ arbitrary.

questions.prompt: Let $\mathbb Z_k$ be the additive group of residue classes modulo $k$. Decide if $\mathbb Z_6$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_3$.
questions.answer: Yes

questions.prompt:
Prove that each rational number $\frac pq\ne0$ can be written in the form
$$\frac pq=b_1+\frac{b_2}{2!}+\dots+\frac{b_n}{n!},$$
where $n$ is a sufficiently large positive integer and $b_k\in\mathbb Z$, with $0\le b_k<k$ for $k>1$, and $b_n\ne0$.
questions.answer: Write $\frac pq=\frac{N}{q!}$ with $N=p\,(q-1)!$ and divide repeatedly with remainder by $q,q-1,\dots,2$ (a "factorial base" expansion); then drop trailing zero digits.

questions.prompt: Decide whether there is a nontrivial homomorphism from the additive group of rational numbers to the additive group of integers.
questions.answer: No

questions.prompt:
Let $A$ be a real magic matrix, i.e. there exists a nonzero real number $S$ such that the sum of each row is equal to $S$, the sum of each column is equal to $S$, the sum of the elements of the main diagonal is equal to $S$ and the sum of the elements of the secondary diagonal is equal to $S$. (Here $A$ is a $3\times3$ matrix, as in part 2.)

1. Prove that if $A$ is invertible then $A^{-1}$ is magic.
2. Show that
$$A=\begin{pmatrix}\frac S3+u&\frac S3-u+v&\frac S3-v\\[2pt] \frac S3-u-v&\frac S3&\frac S3+u+v\\[2pt] \frac S3+v&\frac S3+u-v&\frac S3-u\end{pmatrix},$$
where $u$ and $v$ are arbitrary numbers. Further show that $A$ is not singular if and only if $u^2\ne v^2$.
questions.answer: Every $3\times3$ magic matrix is $A=\frac S3J+M_{u,v}$ (centre $=S/3$ from the four lines through the centre); $M^2=(u^2-v^2)(3I-J)$ and $JM=MJ=0$ give $A^{-1}=\frac1{3S}J+\frac{1}{3(u^2-v^2)}M$, which is of the same magic form, while for $u^2=v^2$ a nonzero vector is killed by $A$. ($\det A=3S(v^2-u^2)$.)

questions.answer: No

questions.prompt:
Let $n\ge1$ and let $m_i$ be natural numbers such that $m_i<p_{n-i}$ $(0\le i\le n-1)$, where $p_k$ is the $k$th prime. Prove that if
$$\frac{m_0}{p_n}+\frac{m_1}{p_{n-1}}+\dots+\frac{m_{n-1}}{2}$$
is a natural number then $m_0=\dots=m_{n-1}=0$.
questions.answer: Multiply by $P=p_1p_2\cdots p_n$ and reduce modulo $p_k$: all terms but one vanish, giving $p_k\mid m_{n-k}$, and $0\le m_{n-k}<p_k$ forces $m_{n-k}=0$.

questions.prompt: Let $P^{(4)}(x)=x^6+x^2+1$. Prove that $P(x)$ does not have ten distinct (real) roots.
questions.answer: By Rolle's theorem, ten distinct real roots of $P$ would give at least six real roots of $P^{(4)}$, but $x^6+x^2+1\ge1>0$ has none.

questions.prompt:
Prove that if $f\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ fulfils the inequalities
$$f(x)\le x,\qquad f(x+y)\le f(x)+f(y)$$
for all $x,y\in\mathbb R$, then $f(x)=x$ for all $x\in\mathbb R$.
questions.answer: $f(0)\le0$ and $f(0)\le2f(0)$ give $f(0)=0$; then $0=f(0)\le f(x)+f(-x)\le x+(-x)=0$ forces $f(x)=x$.

questions.prompt: Prove that an arbitrary integer can be written as a sum of five cubes of integers.
questions.answer: Use $6k=(k+1)^3+(k-1)^3+(-k)^3+(-k)^3$ and $m^3\equiv m\pmod 6$: $m=m^3+6k$ with $k=\frac{m-m^3}{6}\in\mathbb Z$.

questions.prompt:
Prove that for the roots $x_1,x_2$ of the polynomial
$$x^2-px-\frac{1}{2p^2},$$
where $p\in\mathbb R$ and $p\ne0$, the following inequality holds:
$$x_1^4+x_2^4\ge2+\sqrt2 .$$
questions.answer: By Vieta, $x_1^4+x_2^4=2+p^4+\frac{1}{2p^4}$, and AM-GM gives $p^4+\frac1{2p^4}\ge2\sqrt{\frac12}=\sqrt2$.

questions.prompt:
Prove that for all $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$\prod_{i=1}^{n}\left(1+\frac1{2^i}\right)<3 .$$
questions.answer: Using $1+x\le e^x$: the product is $\le e^{\sum 2^{-i}}<e<3$ (or: $\prod_{i\ge2}(1+2^{-i})<\prod(1-2^{-i})^{-1}\le(1-\sum_{i\ge2}2^{-i})^{-1}<2$, then multiply by $\tfrac32$).

$$\big(f(x)-f(y)\big)^2\le|x-y|^3$$
for all $x,y\in\mathbb R$.
questions.answer: No

questions.prompt:
Find a triple of integers $x,y,z$, each greater than $50$ and satisfying
$$x^2+y^2+z^2=3xyz .$$
questions.answer: For example $(x,y,z)=(89,233,62210)$, obtained from $(1,1,1)$ by repeatedly replacing one variable $z$ with $3xy-z$ (Vieta jumping).

questions.prompt:
Prove that for an arbitrary $n\in\mathbb N$, the number
$$\left(\frac{3+\sqrt{17}}{2}\right)^n+\left(\frac{3-\sqrt{17}}{2}\right)^n$$
is an odd integer.
questions.answer: $a_n=\lambda_1^n+\lambda_2^n$ with $\lambda_{1,2}$ the roots of $t^2-3t-2$ satisfies $a_{n+2}=3a_{n+1}+2a_n$, $a_0=2$, $a_1=3$; modulo 2, $a_{n+2}\equiv a_{n+1}$, so $a_n$ is odd for $n\ge1$.

Let the function $f\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfy
$$f(xy)=\frac{f(x)+f(y)}{x+y}$$
for all $x,y\in\mathbb R$ with $x+y\ne0$. Is there $x\in\mathbb R$ such that $f(x)\ne0$?
questions.answer: No

questions.prompt:
How many real roots does the polynomial
$$1+x+\frac{x^2}2+\frac{x^3}3+\dots+\frac{x^n}n$$
have?
questions.answer: Exactly one real root if $n$ is odd and none if $n$ is even ($f'=\frac{x^n-1}{x-1}$; for even $n$ the minimum $f(-1)$ is positive).

questions.prompt:
Discuss the solvability of the system of equations
$$\begin{aligned}\lambda x + y + z &= a\\ x + \lambda y + z &= b\\ x + y + \lambda z &= c\end{aligned}$$
for all numbers $\lambda, a, b, c \in \mathbb R$.
questions.answer: For $\lambda\notin\{1,-2\}$ there is exactly one solution, $x=\frac{(\lambda+1)a-b-c}{(\lambda-1)(\lambda+2)}$ (and cyclically); for $\lambda=1$ it is solvable iff $a=b=c$ (two-parameter family); for $\lambda=-2$ it is solvable iff $a+b+c=0$ (one-parameter family). The determinant is $(\lambda-1)^2(\lambda+2)$.

questions.prompt: Let $f(x)$ be an even twice differentiable function such that $f''(0)\neq 0$. Prove that $f(x)$ has a local extremum at $x=0$.
questions.answer: Evenness forces $f'(0)=0$ (the one-sided difference quotients are negatives of each other); then $f''(0)\ne0$ and the second-derivative test give a strict local extremum.

questions.prompt: Let $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ be mutually inverse decreasing functions on the interval $(0,\infty)$. Can it hold that $f(x)>g(x)$ for all $x\in(0,\infty)$?
questions.answer: Yes

questions.prompt:
Prove that the systems of hyperbolas
$$x^2-y^2=a \qquad (1)$$
$$xy=b \qquad (2)$$
are orthogonal.
questions.answer: The gradients $(2x,-2y)$ of $x^2-y^2$ and $(y,x)$ of $xy$ have dot product $2xy-2xy=0$, so the curves cross at right angles at every intersection point (other than the origin, which only occurs in the degenerate case $a=b=0$).

questions.prompt: Let $f=f_0+f_1z+f_2z^2+\dots+f_{2n}z^{2n}$ and $f_k=f_{2n-k}$ for each $k$. Prove that $f(z)=z^n g\left(z+z^{-1}\right)$, where $g$ is a polynomial of degree $n$.
questions.answer: Pair $z^{n+m}$ with $z^{n-m}$: $z^{-n}f(z)=f_n+\sum_{m=1}^n f_{n+m}(z^m+z^{-m})$, and $z^m+z^{-m}=P_m(z+z^{-1})$ with $P_m$ monic of degree $m$ ($P_{m+1}=wP_m-P_{m-1}$).

questions.prompt: Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous function. Do there exist continuous functions $g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ and $h:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ such that $f(x)=g(x)\sin x+h(x)\cos x$ holds for every $x\in\mathbb R$?
questions.answer: Yes

questions.prompt: Let $\{x_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ be a sequence such that $x_1=25$, $x_n=\arctan x_{n-1}$. Prove that this sequence has a limit and find it.
On the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{z^2}{b^2}=1$ find the point $T=[x_0,z_0]$ such that the triangle bounded by the axes of the ellipse and the tangent at that point has the least area.
questions.answer: $T=\left[\pm\frac{a}{\sqrt2},\pm\frac{b}{\sqrt2}\right]$ (four points, one in each quadrant); the minimal area is $ab$.

questions.answer: No

questions.prompt:
Prove that the equation
$$\frac{z}{1+z^2}+\frac{y}{1+y^2}+\frac{x}{1+x^2}=\frac{1}{1996}$$
has finitely many solutions in positive integers.
questions.answer: Order $x\le y\le z$. Since $t\mapsto\frac t{1+t^2}$ decreases on $[1,\infty)$, $\frac{3x}{1+x^2}\ge\frac1{1996}$ bounds $x$; for each $x$ the remainder bounds $y$; then $z$ solves a quadratic.

questions.prompt: Is it possible to cover the plane with the interiors of a finite number of parabolas?
questions.answer: No

questions.prompt:
Let $\{x_n\}_{n=0}^\infty$ be the sequence such that $x_0=2$, $x_1=1$ and $x_{n+2}$ is the remainder of the number $x_{n+1}+x_n$ divided by $7$. Prove that $x_n$ is the remainder of the number
$$4^n\sum_{k=0}^{[n/2]}2\binom{n}{2k}5^k$$
divided by $7$.
questions.answer: $M_n=2\sum_k\binom n{2k}5^k=(1+\sqrt5)^n+(1-\sqrt5)^n$ satisfies $M_{n+2}=2M_{n+1}+4M_n$; then $y_n=4^nM_n$ satisfies $y_{n+2}\equiv y_{n+1}+y_n\pmod7$ (as $8\equiv64\equiv1$) with $y_0=2$, $y_1\equiv1$, the same as $x_n$.

questions.prompt: Let $\operatorname{cif}(x)$ denote the sum of the digits of the number $x$ in the decimal system. Put $a_1=1997^{1996^{1997}}$, $a_{n+1}=\operatorname{cif}(a_n)$ for every $n>0$. Find $\lim_{n\to\infty}a_n$.
Let $a$ be an odd positive integer. Prove that if $d$ divides $a^2+2$, then $d\equiv1\pmod 8$ or $d\equiv3\pmod 8$.
questions.answer: Every prime $p\mid a^2+2$ is odd with $\left(\frac{-2}{p}\right)=1$, which forces $p\equiv1,3\pmod 8$; the set $\{1,3\}$ of residues mod 8 is closed under multiplication.

questions.prompt:
Let $\alpha\in(0,1]$ be a given real number and let a real sequence $\{a_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ satisfy the inequality
$$a_{n+1}\le\alpha a_n+(1-\alpha)a_{n-1}\qquad\text{for } n=2,3,\dots$$
Prove that if $\{a_n\}$ is bounded, then it must be convergent.
questions.answer: $w_n=a_n+(1-\alpha)a_{n-1}$ is non-increasing and bounded, so $w_n\to W$; then $e_n=a_n-\frac{W}{2-\alpha}$ satisfies $e_n=-(1-\alpha)e_{n-1}+o(1)$ with $0\le1-\alpha<1$, so $a_n\to\frac W{2-\alpha}$.

questions.prompt:
Let $c_1,c_2,\dots,c_n$ be real numbers such that
$$c_1^k+c_2^k+\dots+c_n^k>0\qquad\text{for all }k=1,2,\dots$$
Let us put
$$f(x)=\frac{1}{(1-c_1x)(1-c_2x)\cdots(1-c_nx)}.$$
Show that $f^{(k)}(0)>0$ for all $k=1,2,\dots$
questions.answer: For $g=\ln f=-\sum_j\ln(1-c_jx)$ we get $g^{(m)}(0)=(m-1)!\,p_m>0$ with $p_m=\sum_j c_j^m$; then $f'=fg'$ and Leibniz's rule give $f^{(k+1)}(0)=\sum_{i=0}^k\binom ki f^{(i)}(0)g^{(k+1-i)}(0)>0$ by induction.

questions.prompt:
*(Problem 4-M.)* Find all real numbers $a>0$ for which the series
$$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{a^{f(n)}}{n^2}$$
is convergent; $f(n)$ denotes the number of $0$'s in the decimal expansion of $n$.
questions.answer: Exactly for $0<a<91$. The $m$-digit numbers contribute $9(9+a)^{m-1}$ to $\sum a^{f(n)}$, so the block sums are comparable to $\left(\frac{9+a}{100}\right)^{m}$.

questions.answer: Yes

questions.prompt:
Let $f:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ be a holomorphic function with the property that $|f(z)|=1$ for all $z\in\mathbb C$ such that $|z|=1$. Prove that there exist a $\theta\in\mathbb R$ and a $k\in\{0,1,2,\dots\}$ so that
$$f(z)=e^{i\theta}z^k$$
for all $z\in\mathbb C$.
questions.answer: Divide $f$ by the Blaschke product $B$ of its zeros in the unit disc. Then $|f/B|=1$ on the circle and $f/B$ has no zeros, so max/min principles give $f=e^{i\theta}B$. An entire $f$ forces all zeros to be $0$, so $B=z^k$.

questions.prompt:
Let $u\in C^2(\overline D)$, $u=0$ on $\partial D$, where $D$ is the open unit ball in $\mathbb R^3$. Prove that the following inequality holds for all $\varepsilon>0$:
$$\int_D|\nabla u|^2\,dV\le\varepsilon\int_D(\Delta u)^2\,dV+\frac1{4\varepsilon}\int_Du^2\,dV.$$
(We recall that $\nabla u=\left(\frac{\partial u}{\partial x},\frac{\partial u}{\partial y},\frac{\partial u}{\partial z}\right)$ and $\Delta u=\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial y^2}+\frac{\partial^2u}{\partial z^2}$ are gradient and Laplacian respectively.)
questions.answer: Green's identity with $u|_{\partial D}=0$ gives $\int_D|\nabla u|^2=-\int_Du\,\Delta u$, and $|u\,\Delta u|\le\varepsilon(\Delta u)^2+\frac{u^2}{4\varepsilon}$ pointwise.

questions.prompt:
*(Problem 4-M.)* Prove that
$$\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac{n^2}{(7n)!}=\frac1{7^3}\sum_{k=1}^{2}\sum_{j=0}^{6}e^{\cos(2\pi j/7)}\cdot\cos\left(\frac{2k\pi j}{7}+\sin\frac{2\pi j}{7}\right).$$
questions.answer: $\frac{n^2}{(7n)!}=\frac1{49}\left(\frac1{(7n-2)!}+\frac1{(7n-1)!}\right)$, and the roots-of-unity filter $\sum_{j=0}^6\omega^{jk}e^{\omega^j}=7\sum_{m\equiv-k\ (7)}\frac1{m!}$ with $\omega=e^{2\pi i/7}$; take real parts.

questions.prompt:
*(Problem 4-I.)* Problem *Div₃* is specified as follows:

- *Instance:* a finite string of symbols 0 and 1.
- *Question:* is the given string a binary code of a number divisible by 3?

(It is obvious that there is a program which solves problem *Div₃*, i.e., it outputs the right answer *yes* or *no* for any string of 0's and 1's.)

But you should show that there is no program *Gen-Test-Data* with the specification:

- *Input:* any program $P$.
- *Output:* a finite set $D(P)$ of strings of 0's and 1's such that the program $P$ solves problem *Div₃* iff the program $P$ outputs the correct answer for all inputs from $D(P)$.

*Remark.* You can use the Recursion Theorem, which can be expressed in the following form: For any program *Transf* which transforms programs in some way (i.e., for any given program $P$, it constructs some other program $P'=\textit{Transf}(P)$), there exists a program $P_0$ whose input/output behaviour is not affected by the transformation (i.e., $P_0$ and $\textit{Transf}(P_0)$ yield the same outputs for the same inputs).
questions.answer: If Gen-Test-Data existed, let Transf$(P)$ be the program that answers correctly on $D(P)$ and says *yes* elsewhere. A fixed point $P_0$ passes its own test set $D(P_0)$ but answers *yes* on the infinitely many non-multiples of 3 outside it, a contradiction.

questions.prompt: Let $a$ and $d$ be two positive integers. Prove that there exists a constant $K$ such that every set of $K$ consecutive elements of the arithmetic progression $\{a+nd\}_{n=1}^\infty$ contains at least one number which is not prime.
questions.answer: For a prime $p\nmid d$, any $p$ consecutive terms contain a multiple of $p$; with $K=2p$ there are two distinct multiples of $p$, and at most one of them can equal $p$ itself.

questions.prompt:
Find the limit
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\left(\frac{\left(1+\frac1n\right)^n}{e}\right)^{n}.$$
questions.answer: 1/sqrt(e)

questions.prompt: Give an example of a sequence of continuous functions on $\mathbb R$ converging pointwise to $0$ which is not uniformly convergent on any nonempty open set.
questions.answer: With a tent $g_n$ of height $1$ on $[0,\frac2n]$ peaking at $\frac1n$ and an enumeration $(r_k)$ of $\mathbb Q$, take $f_n(t)=\sum_{k\ge0}2^{-k}g_n(t-r_k)$: each bump slides into its rational and vanishes pointwise, but $f_n(r_k+\frac1n)\ge2^{-k}$.

questions.prompt:
*(Problem 4-M.)* Prove the inequality
$$\frac{n\pi}4-\frac1{\sqrt{8n}}\le\frac12+\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\sqrt{1-\frac{k^2}{n^2}}\le\frac{n\pi}4$$
for every integer $n\ge2$.
questions.answer: Compare $\frac1n\left(\frac12+\sum\right)$ with $\frac\pi4=\int_0^1\sqrt{1-x^2}\,dx$: chord trapezoids of the concave quarter-circle lie below it (upper bound), tangent trapezoids at the points $\frac kn$ lie above it (lower bound), with the error coming from the last half-interval.

questions.prompt: *(Problem 4-I.)* Prove that there exists a program in standard Pascal which prints out its own ASCII code. No disk operations are permitted.
questions.answer: Yes: a self-reproducing program (quine). Store the text of the program, except for the string literals, in string constants, and print them twice, once quoted (writing the quote as `chr(39)`) and once plain. Abstractly, this follows from Kleene's recursion theorem.

questions.prompt: Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space. Let $T:H\to H$ be a bounded linear operator such that $|(Tx,x)|\le\|x\|^2$ for each $x\in H$. Assume that $\mu\in\mathbb C$, $|\mu|=1$, is an eigenvalue with the corresponding eigenspace $E=\{\varphi\in H:T\varphi=\mu\varphi\}$. Prove that the orthogonal complement $E^\perp=\{x\in H:\forall\varphi\in E:(x,\varphi)=0\}$ of $E$ is $T$-invariant, i.e., $T(E^\perp)\subseteq E^\perp$.
questions.answer: For unit $\varphi\in E$, unit $x\in E^\perp$ and $t\in\mathbb C$, $\|\varphi+tx\|^2=1+|t|^2$ while $(T(\varphi+tx),\varphi+tx)=\mu+t(Tx,\varphi)+|t|^2(Tx,x)$. Choosing $t=s\mu\overline{(Tx,\varphi)}/|(Tx,\varphi)|$ with small $s>0$ violates the bound unless $(Tx,\varphi)=0$.

questions.prompt: Decide whether there is a member in the arithmetic sequence $\{a_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ whose first member is $a_1=1998$ and the common difference $d=131$ which is a palindrome (palindrome is a number such that its decimal expansion is symmetric, e.g., 7, 33, 433334, 2135312 and so on).
questions.answer: Yes

questions.prompt: Show that all complex roots of the polynomial $P(z)=a_0z^n+a_1z^{n-1}+\dots+a_{n-1}z+a_n$, where $0<a_0<\dots<a_n$, satisfy $|z|>1$.
questions.answer: $(1-z)P(z)=a_n-\left[a_0z^{n+1}+\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}(a_{j+1}-a_j)z^{n-j}\right]$, and for $|z|\le1$ the bracket has modulus $\le a_0+\sum(a_{j+1}-a_j)=a_n$, with equality only if $z=1$; but $P(1)>0$ (Eneström-Kakeya).

questions.prompt:
*(Problem 4-M.)* A function $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ has the property that for every $x,y\in\mathbb R$ there exists a real number $t$ (depending on $x$ and $y$) such that $0<t<1$ and
$$f\big(tx+(1-t)y\big)=tf(x)+(1-t)f(y).$$
Does it imply that
$$f\left(\frac{x+y}2\right)=\frac{f(x)+f(y)}2$$
for every $x,y\in\mathbb R$?
questions.answer: No

questions.prompt:
*(Problem 4-I.)* Let us consider a first-order language $L$ with a ternary predicate $\mathrm{Plus}$. Hence (well-formed) formulas of $L$ are built of symbols for variables, logical connectives, quantifiers, brackets, and the predicate symbol $\mathrm{Plus}$.
$$(\exists x_1)(\forall x_2)\colon\big(\mathrm{Plus}(x_2,x_1,x_2)\wedge(\forall x_3)\colon\neg\mathrm{Plus}(x_1,x_3,x_3)\big)$$
is an example of such a formula. Recall that a formula is *closed* iff each variable symbol occurs within the scope of a quantifier.

Show that there exists an algorithm which decides whether or not a given closed formula of $L$ is true for the set $\mathbb N$ of natural numbers ($\{0,1,2,\dots\}$) where $\mathrm{Plus}(x,y,z)$ is interpreted as $x+y=z$.
questions.answer: Encode $n$-tuples of naturals as words over $\{0,1\}^n$ (binary, least significant bit first). For every subformula, effectively build a finite automaton accepting the encodings of the tuples satisfying it: atomic $\mathrm{Plus}$ via a carry automaton, $\neg,\wedge,\vee$ by complement/product, $\exists$ by nondeterministically guessing a track plus determinisation. A closed formula then gives an automaton accepting either everything or nothing.

questions.prompt:
Find the limit
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\left(\prod_{k=1}^{n}\frac{k}{k+n}\right)^{\left(e^{\frac{1999}{n}}-1\right)}.$$

Find all natural numbers $n\ge 1$ such that the implication
$$(11\mid a^n+b^n)\implies(11\mid a\ \wedge\ 11\mid b)$$
holds for any two natural numbers $a$ and $b$.
questions.answer: Exactly the **even** $n$. For odd $n$, $a=1$, $b=10$ is a counterexample; for even $n$ use that $-1$ is not a square modulo $11$.

questions.prompt: Let $A_1,\dots,A_n$ be points of an ellipsoid with center $O$ in $\mathbb R^n$ such that $OA_i$, for $i=1,\dots,n$, are mutually orthogonal. Prove that the distance of the point $O$ from the hyperplane $A_1A_2\dots A_n$ does not depend on the choice of the points $A_1,\dots,A_n$.
questions.answer: With the ellipsoid $x^{T}Mx=1$, the distance equals $1/\sqrt{\operatorname{tr}M}$ $=\big(\sum_i a_i^{-2}\big)^{-1/2}$ for semi-axes $a_i$, because $|OA_i|^{-2}=e_i^{T}Me_i$ for the orthonormal directions $e_i$ and the trace does not depend on the basis.

questions.prompt: Show that the following implication holds for any two complex numbers $x$ and $y$: if $x+y,\ x^2+y^2,\ x^3+y^3,\ x^4+y^4\in\mathbb Z$, then $x^n+y^n\in\mathbb Z$ for all natural $n$.
questions.answer: From $2xy=(x+y)^2-(x^2+y^2)$ and $2x^2y^2=(x^2+y^2)^2-(x^4+y^4)$ one gets $xy\in\mathbb Z$; then $s_n=x^n+y^n$ satisfies $s_n=(x+y)s_{n-1}-xy\,s_{n-2}$.

questions.prompt: Find the minimal $k$ such that every set of $k$ different lines in $\mathbb R^3$ contains either $3$ mutually parallel lines or $3$ mutually intersecting lines or $3$ mutually skew lines.

Let $a,b\in\mathbb R$, $a\le b$. Assume that $f\colon[a,b]\to[a,b]$ satisfies $|f(x)-f(y)|\le|x-y|$ for every $x,y\in[a,b]$. Choose an $x_1\in[a,b]$ and define
$$x_{n+1}=\frac{x_n+f(x_n)}{2},\qquad n=1,2,3,\dots.$$
Show that $\{x_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ converges to some fixed point of $f$.
questions.answer: The map $g(x)=\frac{x+f(x)}2$ is non-decreasing (because $f$ is 1-Lipschitz) and maps $[a,b]$ into itself, so $(x_n)$ is monotone and bounded; its limit $L$ satisfies $g(L)=L$, i.e. $f(L)=L$.

questions.prompt: Suppose that we have a countable set $A$ of balls and a unit cube in $\mathbb R^3$. Assume that for every finite subset $B$ of $A$ it is possible to put all balls of $B$ into the cube in such a way that they have disjoint interiors. Show that it is possible to arrange all the balls in the cube so that all of them have pairwise disjoint interiors.
questions.answer: Compactness: arrange the first $n$ balls for every $n$, extract by a diagonal argument a subsequence along which every centre converges, and note that the conditions \"ball inside the cube\" and \"disjoint interiors\" are closed conditions on the centres.

questions.prompt:
Let $u_1,u_2,\dots,u_n\in C([0,1]^n)$ be nonnegative and continuous functions, and let $u_j$ do not depend on the $j$-th variable for $j=1,\dots,n$. Show that
$$\left(\int_{[0,1]^n}\prod_{j=1}^n u_j\right)^{n-1}\le\prod_{j=1}^n\int_{[0,1]^n}u_j^{\,n-1}.$$
questions.answer: Loomis–Whitney-type inequality: induction on $n$; integrate out the last variable using Hölder's inequality for $n$ factors, then apply Hölder with exponents $n,\frac n{n-1}$ and the induction hypothesis.

questions.prompt: Is there a countable set $Y$ and an uncountable family $\mathcal F$ of its subsets such that for every two distinct $A,B\in\mathcal F$, their intersection $A\cap B$ is finite?
questions.answer: Yes

questions.prompt:
Let $f\colon\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$ be given by
$$f(n)=n^{\frac12\tau(n)}$$
for $n\in\mathbb N=\{1,2,\dots\}$, where $\tau(n)$ is the number of divisors of $n$. Show that $f$ is an injection into $\mathbb N$.
questions.answer: $f(n)$ is the product of all divisors of $n$, hence a natural number; if $m^{\tau(m)}=n^{\tau(n)}$ then $m,n$ have proportional prime exponents, so one divides the other, which forces $\tau(m)=\tau(n)$ and $m=n$.

questions.prompt:
Let $a_1,a_2,\dots$ be a bounded sequence of reals. Is it true that the fact
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N a_n=b\qquad\text{and}\qquad\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1{\log N}\sum_{n=1}^N\frac{a_n}{n}=c$$
implies $b=c$?
questions.answer: Yes

questions.prompt: Let us choose arbitrarily $n$ vertices of a regular $2n$-gon and colour them red. The remaining vertices are coloured blue. We arrange all red-red distances into a non-decreasing sequence and do the same with the blue-blue distances. Prove that the sequences are equal.
questions.answer: For each possible distance $d$, double counting pairs (red vertex, vertex at distance $d$) gives $2\,rr_d+rb_d=n\deg_d=2\,bb_d+rb_d$, so the numbers of red-red and blue-blue pairs at distance $d$ agree.

questions.prompt:
Let $p$ be a prime of the form $p=4n-1$ where $n$ is a positive integer. Prove that
$$\prod_{k=1}^p(k^2+1)\equiv4\pmod p.$$
questions.answer: The squares $k^2$ run over $0$ (once) and every quadratic residue $r$ (twice), and $\prod_r(x-r)\equiv x^{(p-1)/2}-1$; at $x=-1$ this gives $\prod_r(r+1)\equiv2$, so the product is $\equiv 2^2=4$.

questions.prompt: If we write the sequence AAABABBB along the perimeter of a circle, then every word of the length $3$ consisting of letters A and B (i.e. AAA, AAB, ABA, BAB, ABB, BBB, BBA, BAA) occurs exactly once on the perimeter. Decide whether it is possible to write a sequence of letters from a $k$-element alphabet along the perimeter of a circle in such a way that every word of the length $l$ (i.e. an ordered $l$-tuple of letters) occurs exactly once on the perimeter.
questions.answer: Yes

questions.prompt:
Let $m,n$ be positive integers and let $x\in[0,1]$. Prove that
$$(1-x^n)^m+\big(1-(1-x)^m\big)^n\ge1.$$
questions.answer: Colour each cell of an $m\times n$ board black with probability $x$ independently: \"some row is all black\" and \"some column is all white\" are disjoint events with probabilities $1-(1-x^n)^m$ and $1-(1-(1-x)^m)^n$.

questions.prompt:
Let $\mathcal B$ be a family of open balls in $\mathbb R^n$ and $c<\lambda\big(\bigcup\mathcal B\big)$ where $\lambda$ is the $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Show that there exists a finite family of pairwise disjoint balls $\{U_i\}_{i=1}^k\subseteq\mathcal B$ such that
$$\sum_{j=1}^k\lambda(U_j)>\frac{c}{3^n}.$$
questions.answer: Vitali covering argument: take a compact $K\subseteq\bigcup\mathcal B$ with $\lambda(K)>c$, cover it by finitely many balls, and greedily pick disjoint balls by decreasing radius; the tripled chosen balls cover $K$.

questions.prompt:
Let $A$ be a set of positive integers such that for any $x,y\in A$
$$x>y\implies x-y\ge\frac{xy}{25}.$$
Find the maximal possible number of elements of the set $A$.

Prove that for any prime $p\ge5$, the number
$$\sum_{0<k<\frac{2p}{3}}\binom pk$$
is divisible by $p^2$.
questions.answer: $\frac1p\binom pk\equiv\frac{(-1)^{k-1}}k\pmod p$, so it suffices that $\sum_{0<k<2p/3}\frac{(-1)^{k-1}}k=\sum_{p/3<k<2p/3}\frac1k\equiv0$, which follows from the symmetry $k\mapsto p-k$.

questions.prompt:
Let $n\ge2$ be a natural number. Prove that
$$\prod_{k=2}^n\ln k<\frac{\sqrt{n!}}{n}.$$
questions.answer: Use $\ln x<\frac{x-1}{\sqrt x}$ for $x>1$ and multiply over $k=2,\dots,n$: $\prod\sqrt k\cdot\prod\frac{k-1}{k}=\frac{\sqrt{n!}}n$.

questions.prompt:
Let $A,B,C$ be nonempty sets in $\mathbb R^n$. Suppose that $A$ is bounded, $C$ is closed and convex, and $A+B\subseteq A+C$. Prove that $B\subseteq C$.

We remind that $E+F=\{e+f:e\in E,\ f\in F\}$ and $D\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is convex iff $tx+(1-t)y\in D$ for all $x,y\in D$ and any $t\in[0,1]$.
questions.answer: Fix $b\in B$, $a_0\in A$ and iterate $a_{i-1}+b=a_i+c_i$; then $b-\frac1i(c_1+\dots+c_i)=\frac{a_i-a_0}i\to0$, the averages lie in $C$ by convexity, and $C$ is closed. (Alternatively, separate $b\notin C$ from $C$ by a linear functional.)

questions.prompt: Let $n\ge2$ be an integer and let $x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n$ be real numbers. Consider $N=\binom n2$ sums $x_i+x_j$, $1\le i<j\le n$, and denote them by $y_1,y_2,\dots,y_N$ (in an arbitrary order). For which $n$ are the numbers $x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n$ uniquely determined by the numbers $y_1,y_2,\dots,y_N$?
questions.answer: Exactly when $n$ is **not a power of $2$**. (Power sums of the $x_i$ can be recovered from those of the $y_j$ via $(2n-2^k)s_k=2t_k-\sum_{r=1}^{k-1}\binom kr s_rs_{k-r}$; for $n=2^m$ there are counterexamples built from $\{0,3\},\{1,2\}$.)

questions.prompt:
Let $f\colon[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous function. Define a sequence of functions $f_n\colon[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ in the following way:
$$f_0(x)=f(x),\qquad f_{n+1}(x)=\int_0^xf_n(t)\,dt,\qquad n=0,1,2,\dots.$$
Prove that if $f_n(1)=0$ for all $n$, then $f(x)\equiv0$.
questions.answer: Integration by parts gives $\int_0^1(1-t)^kf(t)\,dt=k!\,f_k(1)=0$, so $f$ is orthogonal to all polynomials; by Weierstrass $\int_0^1f^2=0$.

questions.prompt: Let $f\colon(0,+\infty)\to(0,+\infty)$ be a decreasing function which satisfies $\int_0^\infty f(x)\,dx<+\infty$. Prove that $\lim_{x\to+\infty}xf(x)=0$.
questions.answer: Since $f$ is decreasing, $\frac x2f(x)\le\int_{x/2}^xf(t)\,dt$, and the right side tends to $0$ because the integral converges.

questions.prompt: Let $R$ be an associative non-commutative ring and let $n>2$ be a fixed natural number. Assume that $x^n=x$ for all $x\in R$. Prove that $xy^{n-1}=y^{n-1}x$ holds for all $x,y\in R$.
questions.answer: $e=y^{n-1}$ is idempotent; $R$ has no nonzero nilpotents ($r^2=0\Rightarrow r=r^{n-2}r^2=0$); and $(ex-exe)^2=0=(xe-exe)^2$, so $ex=exe=xe$.

questions.prompt: Differentiable functions $f_1,\dots,f_n\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ are linearly independent. Prove that there exist at least $n-1$ linearly independent functions among $f_1',\dots,f_n'$.
questions.answer: Differentiation is a linear map on $\operatorname{span}(f_1,\dots,f_n)$ whose kernel consists of constants (dimension $\le1$), so the derivatives span a space of dimension $\ge n-1$.

questions.prompt: Let $p>3$ be a prime number and $n=(2^{2p}-1)/3$. Show that $n$ divides $2^n-2$.
questions.answer: $3n=2^{2p}-1$ and $2p\mid n-1$ (as $n$ is odd and $3(n-1)=4(4^{p-1}-1)\equiv0\pmod p$), so $n\mid 2^{2p}-1\mid 2^{n-1}-1$.

questions.prompt:
Positive numbers $x_1,\dots,x_n$ satisfy
$$\frac1{1+x_1}+\frac1{1+x_2}+\dots+\frac1{1+x_n}=1.$$
Prove that
$$\sqrt{x_1}+\sqrt{x_2}+\dots+\sqrt{x_n}\ge(n-1)\left(\frac1{\sqrt{x_1}}+\frac1{\sqrt{x_2}}+\dots+\frac1{\sqrt{x_n}}\right).$$
questions.answer: Rewrite as $\sum\frac{1+x_k}{\sqrt{x_k}}\cdot\sum\frac1{1+x_k}\ge n\sum\frac1{\sqrt{x_k}}$ and apply Chebyshev's inequality: the sequences $\frac{1+x_k}{\sqrt{x_k}}$ and $\frac1{1+x_k}$ are oppositely ordered.

questions.prompt: The numbers $1,2,\dots,n$ are assigned to the vertices of a regular $n$-gon in an arbitrary order. For each edge compute the product of the two numbers at the endpoints and sum up these products. What is the smallest possible value of this sum?
questions.answer: $\dfrac{n^3+3n^2+5n-6}{6}$ for even $n$ and $\dfrac{n^3+3n^2+5n-3}{6}$ for odd $n$ (i.e. $\frac{4m^3+6m^2+5m-3}3$ for $n=2m$, $\frac{4m^3+12m^2+14m+3}3$ for $n=2m+1$), attained by $\dots,4,n-2,2,n,1,n-1,3,n-3,5,\dots$

questions.prompt:
Find all complex solutions to the system
$$\begin{aligned}(a+ic)^3+(ia+b)^3+(-b+ic)^3&=-6,\\(a+ic)^2+(ia+b)^2+(-b+ic)^2&=6,\\(1+i)a+2ic&=0.\end{aligned}$$
A ring $R$ (not necessarily commutative) contains at least one zero divisor and the number of zero divisors is finite. Prove that $R$ is finite.
questions.answer: Take $u,v\ne0$ with $uv=0$. The additive map $x\mapsto xu$ has image in $\{0\}\cup Z$ (since $(xu)v=0$) and kernel in $\{0\}\cup Z$, so $|R|\le(m+1)^2$ where $m=|Z|$.

questions.prompt:
Let $E$ be the set of all continuous functions $u\colon[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ satisfying
$$u^2(t)\le1+4\int_0^ts\,|u(s)|\,ds,\qquad\forall t\in[0,1].$$
Let $\varphi\colon E\to\mathbb R$ be defined by
$$\varphi(u)=\int_0^1\big(u^2(x)-u(x)\big)\,dx.$$
Prove that $\varphi$ has a maximum value and find it.

Prove that
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}n^2\left(\int_0^1\sqrt[n]{1+x^n}\,dx-1\right)=\frac{\pi^2}{12}.$$
questions.answer: Substituting $y=x^n$ gives $n\int_0^1\big((1+y)^{1/n}-1\big)y^{1/n-1}\,dy\to\int_0^1\frac{\ln(1+y)}y\,dy=\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{(-1)^{k-1}}{k^2}=\frac{\pi^2}{12}$.

questions.prompt: Let $d(k)$ denote the number of all natural divisors of a natural number $k$. Prove that for any natural number $n_0$ the sequence $\left\{d(n^2+1)\right\}_{n=n_0}^{\infty}$ is not strictly monotone.
questions.answer: For even $n$, the divisors of the odd non-square $n^2+1$ pair up as $\{d,(n^2+1)/d\}$ with $d<n$ odd, so $d(n^2+1)\le n$; a strictly increasing sequence of even numbers grows by at least $2$ per step and would eventually exceed this bound, and a strictly decreasing sequence of positive integers is impossible.

questions.prompt:
Let $A=(a_{ij})$ be an $m\times n$ real matrix with at least one non-zero element. For each $i\in\{1,\dots,m\}$, let $R_i=\sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij}$ be the sum of the $i$-th row of the matrix $A$, and for each $j\in\{1,\dots,n\}$, let $C_j=\sum_{i=1}^m a_{ij}$ be the sum of the $j$-th column of the matrix $A$. Prove that there exist indices $k\in\{1,\dots,m\}$ and $l\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ such that
$$a_{kl}>0,\quad R_k\ge 0,\quad C_l\ge 0,$$
or
$$a_{kl}<0,\quad R_k\le 0,\quad C_l\le 0.$$
questions.answer: Assume not and split rows into $R_i\ge0$ / $R_i<0$ and columns into $C_j>0$ / $C_j\le0$; computing the sum of the block (negative rows)×(positive columns) in two ways shows it is both $\le0$ and $\ge0$, which forces all $R_i=C_j=0$, and then any non-zero entry works — a contradiction.

questions.prompt:
Find the limit
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\sqrt{1+2\sqrt{1+3\sqrt{\cdots+(n-1)\sqrt{1+n}}}}\,.$$

Let $A$ and $B$ be complex Hermitian $2\times 2$ matrices having the pairs of eigenvalues $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$ and $(\beta_1,\beta_2)$, respectively. Determine all possible pairs of eigenvalues $(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)$ of the matrix $C=A+B$. (We recall that a matrix $A=(a_{ij})$ is Hermitian if and only if $a_{ij}=\overline{a_{ji}}$ for all $i$ and $j$.)
questions.answer: Ordering $\alpha_1\ge\alpha_2$, $\beta_1\ge\beta_2$, $\gamma_1\ge\gamma_2$: exactly the pairs with $\gamma_1+\gamma_2=\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\beta_1+\beta_2$ and $\max(\alpha_1+\beta_2,\ \alpha_2+\beta_1)\le\gamma_1\le\alpha_1+\beta_1$.

questions.prompt: Two real square matrices $A$ and $B$ satisfy the conditions $A^{2002}=B^{2003}=I$ and $AB=BA$. Prove that $A+B+I$ is invertible. (The symbol $I$ denotes the identity matrix.)
questions.answer: If $(A+B+I)x=0$ then $p(B)x=q(B)x=0$ for the coprime polynomials $p(t)=(t+1)^{2002}-1$ and $q(t)=t^{2003}-1$ (a common root would have $|t|=|t+1|=1$, i.e. $t=e^{\pm2\pi i/3}$, but then $t^{2003}=t^2\ne1$), so $x=0$ by Bézout.

questions.prompt:
Let $\{D_1,D_2,\dots,D_n\}$ be a set of disks in the Euclidean plane. (A disk is a set of points whose distance from the given centre is less than or equal to the given radius.) Let $a_{ij}=S(D_i\cap D_j)$ be the area of $D_i\cap D_j$. Prove that the inequality
$$\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij}x_ix_j\ge 0$$
holds for any real numbers $x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n$.
questions.answer: With indicator functions $\chi_i$ of the disks, $a_{ij}=\int\chi_i\chi_j$, so the quadratic form equals $\int_{\mathbb R^2}\big(\sum_i x_i\chi_i\big)^2\,dx\,dy\ge 0$.

questions.prompt:
Let $\{a_n\}_{n=0}^\infty$ be the sequence of real numbers satisfying $a_0=0$, $a_1=1$ and
$$a_{n+2}=a_{n+1}+\frac{a_n}{2^n}$$
for every $n\ge 0$. Prove that
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}a_n=1+\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac{1}{2^{n(n-1)/2}\prod_{k=1}^n(2^k-1)}.$$
questions.answer: $(a_n)$ is increasing and bounded, and $\lim a_n=1+f(\tfrac12)$ for the generating function $f(z)=\sum a_nz^n$, which satisfies $(1-z)f(z)=z^2f(z/2)+z$; iterating this at $z=2^{-1},2^{-2},\dots$ produces exactly the given series.

questions.prompt:
Let $f,g\colon[0,1]\to(0,+\infty)$ be two continuous functions such that $f$ and $\frac gf$ are increasing. Prove that
$$\int_0^1\frac{\int_0^x f(t)\,dt}{\int_0^x g(t)\,dt}\,dx\le 2\int_0^1\frac{f(t)}{g(t)}\,dt .$$
questions.answer: Chebyshev's integral inequality gives $\frac{\int_0^xf}{\int_0^xg}\le\frac{x}{\int_0^x g/f}$, Cauchy–Schwarz gives $\frac{1}{\int_0^x g/f}\le\frac{4}{x^4}\int_0^x t^2\frac fg$, and integrating in $x$ (Fubini) yields $2\int_0^1\frac fg(1-t^2)\,dt\le2\int_0^1\frac fg$.

questions.prompt: Suppose that $f\colon[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ is a continuously differentiable function such that $f(0)=f(1)=0$ and $f(a)=\sqrt3$ for some $a\in(0,1)$. Prove that there exist two tangents to the graph of $f$ that form an equilateral triangle with an appropriate segment of the $x$-axis.
questions.answer: At a maximum point $b$, $f'(b)=0$, while by the mean value theorem $f'$ exceeds $\sqrt3$ somewhere in $(0,b)$ and is below $-\sqrt3$ somewhere in $(b,1)$; by continuity of $f'$ there are points with slopes $\pm\sqrt3$, and the tangents there (inclined at $60^\circ$ and $120^\circ$) cut the $x$-axis in an equilateral triangle.

questions.prompt:
Evaluate the sum
$$\sum_{n=0}^\infty\operatorname{arctg}\left(\frac{1}{1+n+n^2}\right).$$
questions.answer: pi/2

questions.prompt: Denote by $B(c,r)$ the open disk of center $c$ and radius $r$ in the plane. Decide whether there exists a sequence $\{z_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ of points in $\mathbb R^2$ such that the open disks $B(z_n,1/n)$ are pairwise disjoint and the sequence $\{z_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ is convergent.
questions.answer: Yes

questions.prompt: Find all pairs $(m,n)$ of positive integers such that $m+n$ and $mn+1$ are both powers of $2$.
Are the groups $(\mathbb Q,+)$ and $(\mathbb Q^+,\cdot)$ isomorphic? (The symbol $\mathbb Q^+$ denotes the set of all positive rational numbers.)
questions.answer: No

questions.prompt:
Find all functions $f\colon\mathbb R_0^+\times\mathbb R_0^+\to\mathbb R_0^+$ such that

1. $f(x,0)=f(0,x)=x$ for all $x\in\mathbb R_0^+$,
2. $f(f(x,y),z)=f(x,f(y,z))$ for all $x,y,z\in\mathbb R_0^+$ and
3. there exists a real $k$ such that $f(x+y,x+z)=kx+f(y,z)$ for all $x,y,z\in\mathbb R_0^+$.

(The symbol $\mathbb R_0^+$ denotes the set of all non-negative real numbers.)
questions.answer: $f(x,y)=x+y$ and $f(x,y)=\max\{x,y\}$. (Conditions 1 and 3 force $f(x,y)=(k-1)\min\{x,y\}+\max\{x,y\}$, and associativity forces $k\in\{1,2\}$.)

questions.prompt:
Let $\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n$ be a divergent series with positive non-increasing terms. Prove that the series
$$\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac{a_n}{1+na_n}$$
diverges.
questions.answer: If $na_n<1$ from some point on, the terms are $\ge a_n/2$; otherwise $na_n\ge1$ for infinitely many $n$, and for each such $n$ monotonicity gives $\sum_{n/2<k\le n}\frac{a_k}{1+ka_k}\ge\frac14$, so the Cauchy criterion fails.

questions.prompt:
Let $f\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be an infinitely differentiable function. Assume that for every $x\in\mathbb R$ there is an $n\in\mathbb N$ (depending on $x$) such that
$$f^{(n)}(x)=0 .$$
Prove that $f$ is a polynomial.
questions.answer: Baire category: the closed sets $E_n=\{f^{(n)}=0\}$ cover $\mathbb R$, so $f$ is a polynomial on a dense union of maximal open intervals; the closed complement $H$ has no isolated points, and a second application of Baire on $H$ shows that $H\ne\emptyset$ is impossible.

questions.prompt: Let $S_0=\{z\in\mathbb C: |z|=1,\ z\ne-1\}$ and $f(z)=\operatorname{Im}z/(1+\operatorname{Re}z)$. Prove that $f$ is a bijection between $S_0$ and $\mathbb R$. Find $f^{-1}$.
questions.answer: Writing $z=e^{it}$, $t\in(-\pi,\pi)$, gives $f(z)=\tan\frac t2$, a bijection onto $\mathbb R$; the inverse is $f^{-1}(y)=\dfrac{1+iy}{1-iy}=\dfrac{1-y^2}{1+y^2}+\dfrac{2y}{1+y^2}\,i$.

questions.prompt:
Let $f\colon A^3\to A$ where $A$ is a nonempty set and $f$ satisfies:

(a) for all $x,y\in A$, $f(x,y,y)=x=f(y,y,x)$ and

(b) for all $x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_2,y_3,z_1,z_2,z_3\in A$,
$$f\big(f(x_1,x_2,x_3),f(y_1,y_2,y_3),f(z_1,z_2,z_3)\big)=f\big(f(x_1,y_1,z_1),f(x_2,y_2,z_2),f(x_3,y_3,z_3)\big).$$

Prove that for an arbitrary fixed $a\in A$, the operation $x+y=f(x,a,y)$ is an Abelian group addition.
questions.answer: Write $a=f(a,a,a)$, $x=f(x,a,a)=f(a,a,x)$ and use (b) to "transpose" $3\times3$ arrays: this gives the neutral element $a$, associativity, commutativity, and the inverse $-x=f(a,x,a)$.

questions.prompt:
Find all reals $\lambda$ for which there is a nonzero polynomial $P$ with real coefficients such that
$$\frac{P(1)+P(3)+P(5)+\dots+P(2n-1)}{n}=\lambda P(n)$$
for all positive integers $n$, and find all such polynomials for $\lambda=2$.
questions.answer: $\lambda\in\left\{\dfrac{2^k}{k+1}: k=0,1,2,\dots\right\}=\{1,\tfrac43,2,\tfrac{16}5,\dots\}$; for $\lambda=2$ the polynomials are $P(x)=c\,(x^3-x)$, $c\ne0$.

questions.prompt:
Let $(x_n)_{n\ge2}$ be a sequence of real numbers such that $x_2>0$ and $x_{n+1}=-1+\sqrt[n]{1+nx_n}$ for $n\ge2$. Find

(a) $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}x_n$,

(b) $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}nx_n$.
questions.answer: (a) $0$; (b) $0$. (Bernoulli's inequality shows $x_n$ decreases to $0$; then Stolz–Cesàro with $x_n-x_{n+1}\ge\frac{n-1}2x_{n+1}^2$ gives $nx_n\to0$.)

questions.prompt:
For an arbitrary square matrix $M$, define
$$\exp(M)=I+\frac{M}{1!}+\frac{M^2}{2!}+\frac{M^3}{3!}+\cdots .$$
Construct $2\times2$ matrices $A$ and $B$ such that $\exp(A+B)\ne\exp(A)\exp(B)$.
questions.answer: E.g. $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$, $B=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$: $\exp(A)\exp(B)=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ but $\exp(A+B)=\begin{pmatrix}\cosh1&\sinh1\\\sinh1&\cosh1\end{pmatrix}$.

questions.prompt:
Let $(a_{i,j})_{i,j=1}^n$ be a real matrix such that $a_{i,i}=0$ for $i=1,2,\dots,n$. Prove that there exists a set $\mathcal J\subset\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ of indices such that
$$\sum_{\substack{i\in\mathcal J\\ j\notin\mathcal J}}a_{i,j}+\sum_{\substack{i\notin\mathcal J\\ j\in\mathcal J}}a_{i,j}\ge\frac12\sum_{i,j=1}^na_{i,j}.$$
questions.answer: Take $\mathcal J$ maximising the left side $F(\mathcal J)$; comparing with $\mathcal J\setminus\{k\}$ and $\mathcal J\cup\{k\}$ shows each diagonal block sums to at most $\frac12F(\mathcal J)$. (Alternatively: a random $\mathcal J$ has expected value exactly $\frac12\sum a_{i,j}$.)

questions.prompt:
Let $f\colon[0,1]\times[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous function. Find the limit
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\left(\frac{(2n+1)!}{(n!)^2}\right)^2\int_0^1\int_0^1\big(xy(1-x)(1-y)\big)^nf(x,y)\,dx\,dy .$$
questions.answer: $f\left(\tfrac12,\tfrac12\right)$ — the weights $\big(\frac{(2n+1)!}{(n!)^2}\big)^2(xy(1-x)(1-y))^n$ are probability densities concentrating at $(\frac12,\frac12)$.

questions.prompt:
Let $R$ be a finite ring with the following property: for any $a,b\in R$ there exists an element $c\in R$ (depending on $a$ and $b$) such that $a^2+b^2=c^2$. Prove that for any $a,b,c\in R$ there exists $d\in R$ such that $2abc=d^2$.

(Here $2abc$ denotes $abc+abc$. The ring $R$ is assumed to be associative, but not necessarily commutative and not necessarily containing a unit.)
questions.answer: The set $S$ of squares is closed under addition, hence (by finiteness) an additive subgroup; $xy+yx=(x+y)^2-x^2-y^2\in S$, and $2abc=(abc+bca)+(cab+abc)-(cab+bca)\in S$.

questions.prompt:
Given real numbers $0=x_1<x_2<\dots<x_{2n}<x_{2n+1}=1$ such that $x_{i+1}-x_i\le h$ for $1\le i\le 2n$, show that
$$\frac{1-h}{2}<\sum_{i=1}^nx_{2i}(x_{2i+1}-x_{2i-1})<\frac{1+h}{2}.$$

Suppose that $(a_n)$ is a sequence of real numbers such that the series
$$\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac{a_n}{n}$$
is convergent. Show that the sequence
$$b_n=\frac{\sum_{j=1}^na_j}{n}$$
is convergent and find its limit.

Two players play the following game: Let $n$ be a fixed integer greater than $1$. Starting from number $k=2$, each player has two possible moves: either replace the number $k$ by $k+1$ or by $2k$. The player who is forced to write a number greater than $n$ loses the game. Which player has a winning strategy for which $n$?
questions.answer: The second player wins exactly when all base-4 digits of $n$ are $0$ or $2$ ($n=2,8,10,32,34,40,42,128,\dots$); for all other $n$ the first player wins.

questions.prompt:
Let $A=[a_{ij}]_{n\times n}$ be a matrix with nonnegative entries such that
$$\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^na_{ij}=n .$$

(a) Prove that $|\det A|\le1$.

(b) If $|\det A|=1$ and $\lambda\in\mathbb C$ is an arbitrary eigenvalue of $A$, show that $|\lambda|=1$.

(We call $\lambda\in\mathbb C$ an eigenvalue of $A$ if there exists a nonzero vector $x\in\mathbb C^n$ such that $Ax=\lambda x$.)
questions.answer: $|\det A|\le\sum_\sigma\prod_i a_{i\sigma(i)}\le\prod_i r_i\le\big(\frac1n\sum r_i\big)^n=1$ (row sums $r_i$, AM-GM); equality forces $A$ to be a permutation matrix, so $A^{m}=I$ for some $m$ and every eigenvalue is a root of unity.

questions.prompt:
(a) Let $u$ and $v$ be two nilpotent elements in a commutative ring (with or without unity). Prove that $u+v$ is also nilpotent. (An element $u$ is called nilpotent if there exists a positive integer $n$ for which $u^n=0$.)

(b) Show an example of a (non-commutative) ring $R$ and nilpotent elements $u,v\in R$ such that $u+v$ is not nilpotent.
questions.answer: (a) If $u^n=v^m=0$, every term of the binomial expansion of $(u+v)^{n+m}$ contains $u^i$ with $i\ge n$ or $v^j$ with $j\ge m$. (b) In $2\times2$ matrices, $u=E_{12}$, $v=E_{21}$ have $u^2=v^2=0$ but $(u+v)^2=I$.

questions.prompt: Let $(G,\cdot)$ be a finite group of order $n$. Show that each element of $G$ is a square if and only if $n$ is odd.
questions.answer: If $n$ is odd, every $g$ has odd order $m$ and $g=(g^{(m+1)/2})^2$. If $n$ is even, there is an element $t$ of order $2$ (pair each element with its inverse), so $t^2=1^2$ and the squaring map is not injective, hence (by finiteness) not surjective.

questions.prompt:
For a function $f\colon[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ the secant of $f$ at points $a,b\in[0,1]$, $a<b$, is the line in $\mathbb R^2$ passing through $(a,f(a))$ and $(b,f(b))$. A function is said to intersect its secant at $a,b$ if there exists a point $c\in(a,b)$ such that $(c,f(c))$ lies on the secant of $f$ at $a,b$.

1. Find the set $\mathcal F$ of all continuous functions $f$ such that for any $a,b\in[0,1]$, $a<b$, the function $f$ intersects its secant at $a,b$.
2. Does there exist a continuous function $f\notin\mathcal F$ such that for any rational $a,b\in[0,1]$, $a<b$, the function $f$ intersects its secant at $a,b$?
questions.answer: 1. $\mathcal F$ consists exactly of the affine functions $f(x)=\alpha x+\beta$. 2. Yes: e.g. $f(x)=\sum_k4^{-k}h(x-q_k)$ with $h(t)=\sqrt{|t|}\sin\ln|t|$ and $(q_k)$ an enumeration of $\mathbb Q\cap[0,1]$; its right difference quotients at every rational point take arbitrarily large values of both signs.

questions.prompt:
Let $f\colon[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be a strictly convex continuous function such that
$$\lim_{x\to+\infty}\frac{f(x)}{x}=+\infty .$$
Prove that the improper integral $\int_0^{+\infty}\sin\big(f(x)\big)\,dx$ is convergent but not absolutely convergent.
questions.answer: Eventually $f$ increases to $\infty$ with right derivative $\to\infty$; with $x_k=f^{-1}(k\pi)$ the integral becomes an alternating series $\sum(-1)^kI_k$ where, by concavity of $f^{-1}$, $I_k$ decreases to $0$ (Leibniz) while $I_k\ge\frac13(x_{k+2}-x_{k+1})$ with $x_k\to\infty$, so $\sum I_k=\infty$.

questions.prompt:
Can the set of positive rationals be split into two nonempty disjoint subsets $Q_1$ and $Q_2$ such that both are closed under addition, i.e. $p+q\in Q_k$ for every $p,q\in Q_k$, $k=1,2$?

Can it be done when addition is exchanged for multiplication, i.e. $p\cdot q\in Q_k$ for every $p,q\in Q_k$, $k=1,2$?
questions.answer: No; yes

questions.prompt: Alice has got a circular key ring with $n$ keys, $n\ge 3$. When she takes it out of her pocket, she does not know whether it got rotated and/or flipped. The only way she can distinguish the keys is by colouring them (a colour is assigned to each key). What is the minimum number of colours needed?
questions.answer: Three colours for $n=3,4,5$; two colours for $n\ge 6$.

questions.prompt: A function $f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$ is called *slowly changing* if for any $t>1$ the limit $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{f(tx)}{f(x)}$ exists and is equal to $1$. Is it true that every slowly changing function has for sufficiently large $x$ a constant sign (i.e., is it true that for every slowly changing $f$ there exists an $N$ such that for every $x,y>N$ we have $f(x)f(y)>0$)?
questions.answer: Yes

questions.prompt:
Let $f:[0,1]\to[0,\infty)$ be an arbitrary function satisfying
$$\frac{f(x)+f(y)}{2}\le f\left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right)+1$$
for all pairs $x,y\in[0,1]$. Prove that for all $0\le u<v<w\le1$,
$$\frac{w-v}{w-u}\,f(u)+\frac{v-u}{w-u}\,f(w)\le f(v)+2.$$
questions.answer: Let $M=\sup_v\big(L(v)-f(v)\big)$, where $L$ is the chord through $(u,f(u))$ and $(w,f(w))$; reflecting $v$ in the nearer endpoint and using the hypothesis gives $M\le \frac M2+1$, so $M\le2$.

questions.prompt: Construct a set $A\subset[0,1]\times[0,1]$ such that $A$ is dense in $[0,1]\times[0,1]$ and every vertical and every horizontal line intersects $A$ in at most one point.
questions.answer: E.g. choose points one by one in the countably many rational open squares, each time avoiding the finitely many $x$- and $y$-coordinates used so far; or take $A=\{(\{n\sqrt2\},\{n\sqrt3\}):n\in\mathbb N\}$.

questions.prompt:
Let $A$ be a real $n\times n$ matrix satisfying
$$A+A^t=I,$$
where $A^t$ denotes the transpose of $A$ and $I$ the $n\times n$ identity matrix. Show that $\det A>0$.
questions.answer: $A=\frac12I+S$ with $S$ skew-symmetric; the eigenvalues of $S$ are $0$ or conjugate pairs $\pm ir$, so $\det A=\left(\tfrac12\right)^{n-2s}\prod\left(\tfrac14+r_k^2\right)>0$.

questions.prompt:
Let $f:[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous function such that $f(0)=f(1)=0$. Prove that the set
$$A:=\{h\in[0,1] : f(x+h)=f(x)\text{ for some }x\in[0,1]\}$$
is Lebesgue measurable and has Lebesgue measure at least $\frac12$.
questions.answer: $A$ is compact; for every $h$, the function $g(x)=f(x+h)-f(x)$ taken cyclically (indices mod $1$) has a zero, so $h\in A$ or $1-h\in A$; hence $A\cup(1-A)=[0,1]$ and $2\lambda(A)\ge1$.

questions.prompt:
Let $S$ be a finite set with $n$ elements and $\mathcal F$ a family of subsets of $S$ with the following property:
$$A\in\mathcal F,\ A\subseteq B\subseteq S\ \Longrightarrow\ B\in\mathcal F.$$
Prove that the function $f:[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ given by
$$f(t):=\sum_{A\in\mathcal F}t^{|A|}(1-t)^{|S\setminus A|}$$
is nondecreasing ($|A|$ denotes the number of elements of $A$).
questions.answer: $f(t)$ is the probability that the random set $X_t=\{j: U_j<t\}$ ($U_j$ independent uniform on $[0,1]$) lies in $\mathcal F$; $X_{t_1}\subseteq X_{t_2}$ for $t_1<t_2$ and $\mathcal F$ is up-closed.

questions.prompt:
Find all complex roots (with multiplicities) of the polynomial
$$p(x)=\sum_{n=1}^{2008}\big(1004-|1004-n|\big)x^n .$$
questions.answer: $p(x)=x\left(1+x+\dots+x^{1003}\right)^2$: the simple root $0$ and the double roots $e^{\pi i k/502}$, $k=1,2,\dots,1003$.

questions.prompt:
Find all functions $f:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ such that
$$f(f(f(x)))+4f(f(x))+f(x)=6x .$$
questions.answer: Only $f(x)=x$ (iterate $f$: the orbit satisfies a linear recurrence with characteristic roots $1,-2,-3$; positivity kills the oscillating terms).

questions.prompt:
Find all $c\in\mathbb R$ for which there exists an infinitely differentiable function $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ such that for all $n\in\mathbb N$ and $x\in\mathbb R$ we have
$$f^{(n+1)}(x)>f^{(n)}(x)+c .$$
questions.answer: Exactly $c\le0$ (e.g. $f(x)=e^{2x}$); for $c>0$, using only $n=1,2$ one shows $f'\to+\infty$ as $x\to-\infty$ while $f'<-\frac{3c}2$ there.

questions.prompt:
The numbers of the set $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ are colored with $6$ colors. Let
$$S:=\{(x,y,z)\in\{1,2,\dots,n\}^3 : x+y+z\equiv0 \pmod n\text{ and }x,y,z\text{ have the same color}\}$$
and
$$D:=\{(x,y,z)\in\{1,2,\dots,n\}^3 : x+y+z\equiv0 \pmod n\text{ and }x,y,z\text{ have three different colors}\}.$$
Prove that
$$|D|\le 2|S|+\frac{n^2}{2}.$$
(For a set $A$, $|A|$ denotes the number of elements in $A$.)
questions.answer: With $n_u$ the size of colour class $u$, double counting gives $|S|-\frac12|D|=\sum n_u^2-\sum_{u<v}n_un_v=\frac32\sum n_u^2-\frac12n^2\ge-\frac{n^2}4$.

questions.prompt:
Find all functions $f:\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z$ such that
$$19f(x)-17f(f(x))=2x$$
for all $x\in\mathbb Z$.
questions.answer: Only $f(x)=x$: with $g(x)=x-f(x)$ one gets $2g(x)=17g(f(x))$, so $17^k\mid g(x)$ for all $k$.

questions.prompt:
Find all continuously differentiable functions $f:[0,1]\to(0,\infty)$ such that $\dfrac{f(1)}{f(0)}=e$ and
$$\int_0^1\frac{dx}{f(x)^2}+\int_0^1f'(x)^2\,dx\le2 .$$
questions.answer: Only $f(x)=\sqrt{2x+\dfrac{2}{e^2-1}}$ (expand $\int_0^1\left(f'-\frac1f\right)^2\ge0$; equality forces $ff'=1$).

questions.prompt: Find all pairs of natural numbers $(n,m)$ with $1<n<m$ such that the numbers $1$, $\sqrt[n]{n}$ and $\sqrt[m]{m}$ are linearly dependent over the field of rational numbers $\mathbb Q$.

We consider the following game for one person. The aim of the player is to reach a fixed capital $C>2$. The player begins with capital $0<x_0<C$. In each turn let $x$ be the player's current capital. Define $s(x)$ as follows:
$$s(x):=\begin{cases}x & \text{if } x<1,\\ C-x & \text{if } C-x<1,\\ 1 & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$$
Then a fair coin is tossed and the player's capital either increases or decreases by $s(x)$, each with probability $\frac12$. Find the probability that in a finite number of turns the player wins by reaching the capital $C$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{x_0}{C}$.

questions.prompt: Let $ABC$ be a non-degenerate triangle in the Euclidean plane. Define a sequence $(C_n)_{n=0}^\infty$ of points as follows: $C_0:=C$, and $C_{n+1}$ is the center of the incircle of the triangle $ABC_n$. Find $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}C_n$.
questions.answer: The point $L$ on segment $AB$ with $AL:LB=\beta:\alpha$, i.e. $L=\dfrac{\alpha A+\beta B}{\alpha+\beta}$, where $\alpha,\beta$ are the angles of $ABC$ at $A$ and $B$.

questions.prompt:
Prove that the number
$$2^{2^k-1}-2^k-1$$
is composite (not prime) for all positive integers $k>2$.
questions.answer: For even $k$ the number is divisible by $3$; for odd $k$ write $k+1=2^aq$ ($q$ odd): the Fermat number $2^{2^a}+1$ divides both $2^{2^k}-1$ and $2^{k+1}+1$, hence $2M$ and $M$.

questions.prompt:
Let $k$ and $n$ be positive integers such that $k\le n-1$. Let $S:=\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ and let $A_1,A_2,\dots,A_k$ be nonempty subsets of $S$. Prove that it is possible to color some elements of $S$ using two colors, red and blue, such that the following conditions are satisfied:

1. Each element of $S$ is either left uncolored or is colored red or blue.
2. At least one element of $S$ is colored.
3. Each set $A_i$ ($i=1,2,\dots,k$) is either completely uncolored or it contains at least one red and at least one blue element.
questions.answer: Take a nonzero solution of the $k<n$ homogeneous equations $\sum_{j\in A_i}x_j=0$ and colour $j$ red if $x_j>0$, blue if $x_j<0$.

questions.prompt:
Let $(a_n)_{n=1}^\infty$ be a sequence of real numbers. We say that the sequence $(a_n)_{n=1}^\infty$ *covers the set of positive integers* if for any positive integer $m$ there exists a positive integer $k$ such that $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n^k=m$.

a) Does there exist a sequence of real positive numbers which covers the set of positive integers?

b) Does there exist a sequence of real numbers which covers the set of positive integers?
questions.answer: No; yes

questions.prompt:
A positive integer $m$ is called *self-descriptive in base $b$*, where $b\ge2$ is an integer, if:

1. The representation of $m$ in base $b$ is of the form $(a_0a_1\dots a_{b-1})_b$ (that is $m=a_0b^{b-1}+a_1b^{b-2}+\dots+a_{b-2}b+a_{b-1}$, where $0\le a_i\le b-1$ are integers).
2. $a_i$ is equal to the number of occurrences of the number $i$ in the sequence $(a_0a_1\dots a_{b-1})$.

For example, $(1210)_4$ is self-descriptive in base $4$, because it has four digits and contains one $0$, two $1$s, one $2$ and no $3$s.

a) Find all bases $b\ge2$ such that no number is self-descriptive in base $b$.

b) Prove that if $x$ is a self-descriptive number in base $b$ then the last (least significant) digit of $x$ is $0$.
questions.answer: (a) $b\in\{2,3,6\}$ (examples: $1210_4$, $21200_5$, and $(b-4)\,2\,1\,0\cdots0\,1\,000$ for $b\ge7$). (b) If $a_{b-1}\ge1$, some digit equals $b-1$, and the digit sum $b$ leaves no room for $b-1$ equal digits.

questions.prompt:
Let $E$ be the set of all continuously differentiable real valued functions $f$ on $[0,1]$ such that $f(0)=0$ and $f(1)=1$. Define
$$J(f)=\int_0^1(1+x^2)\big(f'(x)\big)^2\,dx .$$
a) Show that $J$ achieves its minimum value at some element of $E$.

b) Calculate $\displaystyle\min_{f\in E}J(f)$.
questions.answer: 4/pi

questions.prompt:
Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ square matrix with integer entries. Suppose that $p^2A^{p^2}=q^2A^{q^2}+r^2I_n$ for some positive integers $p,q,r$ where $r$ is odd and $p^2=q^2+r^2$. Prove that $|\det A|=1$.

(Here $I_n$ means the $n\times n$ identity matrix.)
questions.answer: Every eigenvalue $\lambda$ is a root of $f(x)=p^2x^{p^2}-q^2x^{q^2}-r^2$, so $f(|\lambda|)\le0$, which forces $0<|\lambda|\le1$; hence $0<|\det A|\le1$ and the integer $\det A$ is $\pm1$.

questions.prompt:
Let $k,m,n$ be positive integers such that $1\le m\le n$ and denote $S=\{1,2,\dots,n\}$. Suppose that $A_1,A_2,\dots,A_k$ are $m$-element subsets of $S$ with the following property: for every $i=1,2,\dots,k$ there exists a partition $S=S_{1,i}\cup S_{2,i}\cup\dots\cup S_{m,i}$ (into pairwise disjoint subsets) such that

1. $A_i$ has precisely one element in common with each member of the above partition.
2. Every $A_j$, $j\neq i$, is disjoint from at least one member of the above partition.

Show that $k\le\dbinom{n-1}{m-1}$.
questions.answer: Polynomial method: $P_i=\prod_{l=2}^m\sum_{s\in S_{l,i}}x_s$ (with $1\in S_{1,i}$) are multilinear of degree $m-1$ in $x_2,\dots,x_n$, and the matrix $P_i(\chi_{A_j})$ is the identity mod $2$, so they are linearly independent.

questions.prompt:
a) Is it true that for every bijection $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ the series
$$\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac{1}{n\,f(n)}$$
is convergent?

b) Prove that there exists a bijection $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ such that the series
$$\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac{1}{n+f(n)}$$
is convergent.

($\mathbb N$ is the set of all positive integers.)
questions.answer: (a) Yes: $\frac1{nf(n)}\le\frac12\left(\frac1{n^2}+\frac1{f(n)^2}\right)$, so the sum is at most $\frac{\pi^2}6$. (b) E.g. swap the $j$-th number that is not a power of $2$ with $2^j$; then the series is $\sum_j\frac{2}{x_j+2^j}<2$.

questions.prompt: Let $A$ and $B$ be two complex $2\times2$ matrices such that $AB-BA=B^2$. Prove that $AB=BA$.
questions.answer: $\operatorname{tr}B^2=\operatorname{tr}(AB-BA)=0$; with Cayley–Hamilton $B^2=(\operatorname{tr}B)B-(\det B)I$ this forces $B^2=0$, so $AB-BA=0$.

questions.prompt:
Prove that there exist positive constants $c_1$ and $c_2$ with the following properties:

a) For all real $k>1$,
$$\left|\int_0^1\sqrt{1-x^2}\cos(kx)\,dx\right|<\frac{c_1}{k^{3/2}} .$$

b) For all real $k>1$,
$$\left|\int_0^1\sqrt{1-x^2}\sin(kx)\,dx\right|>\frac{c_2}{k} .$$
questions.answer: Integrate by parts once, split $\int_0^1 f'(x)\,g(kx)\,dx$ at $\sqrt{1-1/k}$ (by parts again on the left, trivial bound on the right) to get $O(k^{-1/2})$; this gives $c_1=3$ and $\int f\sin kx=\frac1k+O(k^{-3/2})$, plus positivity for small $k$.

questions.prompt:
For every positive integer $n$ let $\sigma(n)$ denote the sum of all its positive divisors. A number $n$ is called *weird* if $\sigma(n)\ge2n$ and there exists no representation
$$n=d_1+d_2+\dots+d_r,$$
where $r>1$ and $d_1,\dots,d_r$ are pairwise distinct positive divisors of $n$.

Prove that there are infinitely many weird numbers.
questions.answer: $70$ is weird, and if $n$ is weird and $p>\sigma(n)$ is prime then $pn$ is weird; infinitely many primes give infinitely many weird numbers.

questions.prompt:
Let $a$ and $b$ be given positive coprime integers. Then for every integer $n$ there exist integers $x,y$ such that
$$n=ax+by .$$
Prove that $n=ab$ is the greatest integer for which $xy\le0$ in all such representations of $n$.
questions.answer: For $n=ab$: $a\mid y$, $b\mid x$, so $x>0$ forces $x\ge b$ and $y\le0$. For $n>ab$: the representation with $1\le x\le b$ has $by=n-ax\ge n-ab>0$.

questions.prompt: Prove or disprove that if a real sequence $(a_n)$ satisfies $a_{n+1}-a_n\to0$ and $a_{2n}-2a_n\to0$ as $n\to\infty$, then $a_n\to0$.
questions.answer: True

questions.prompt:
Let $A$ and $B$ be two $n\times n$ matrices with integer entries such that all of the matrices
$$A,\quad A+B,\quad A+2B,\quad A+3B,\quad\dots,\quad A+(2n)B$$
are invertible and their inverses have integer entries, too. Show that $A+(2n+1)B$ is also invertible and that its inverse has integer entries.
questions.answer: $P(t)=\det(A+tB)$ is a polynomial of degree $\le n$ taking values $\pm1$ at the $2n+1$ points $0,\dots,2n$; one value is taken $n+1$ times, so $P$ is constant $\pm1$; then the adjugate formula gives an integer inverse.

questions.prompt:
Let $f:[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ be a function satisfying
$$|f(x)-f(y)|\le|x-y|$$
for every $x,y\in[0,1]$. Show that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists a countable family of rectangles $(R_i)$ of dimensions $a_i\times b_i$, $a_i\le b_i$, in the plane such that
$$\{(x,f(x)) : x\in[0,1]\}\subset\bigcup_iR_i\qquad\text{and}\qquad\sum_ia_i<\varepsilon .$$
(The edges of the rectangles are not necessarily parallel to the coordinate axes.)
questions.answer: Call $[x,y]$ *$\eta$-flat* if the graph over it stays within $\eta(y-x)$ of the chord; any non-flat interval contains a subinterval of proportional length whose slope is larger by $\eta$, so after at most $1/\eta$ steps one finds a flat subinterval of length $\ge c|I|$. Exhaust $[0,1]$ by flat intervals (thin rectangles along chords, total width $\le2\eta$) up to a remainder of small length (covered by small squares).

questions.prompt:
**(a)** Is there a polynomial $P(x)$ with real coefficients such that
$$P\left(\frac1k\right)=\frac{k+2}{k}$$
for all positive integers $k$?

**(b)** Is there a polynomial $P(x)$ with real coefficients such that
$$P\left(\frac1k\right)=\frac{1}{2k+1}$$
for all positive integers $k$?

(Answer with two words: one for (a), one for (b).)
questions.answer: (a) Yes; (b) No

questions.prompt: Let $(a_n)_{n=1}^\infty$ be an unbounded and strictly increasing sequence of positive reals such that the arithmetic mean of any four consecutive terms $a_n,a_{n+1},a_{n+2},a_{n+3}$ belongs to the same sequence. Prove that the sequence $a_{n+1}/a_n$ converges and find all possible values of its limit.
questions.answer: 1+sqrt(2)

Expand $\frac1{(1-u)^2}=\sum(j+1)u^j$ and swap sums: the left side becomes $\sum_j\frac{(2j+1)x^{2j}}{1-x^{2j+1}}=-\frac{d}{dx}\sum_j\ln(1-x^{2j+1})$, the right side $\sum_j\frac{(j+1)x^j}{1+x^{j+1}}=\frac{d}{dx}\sum_j\ln(1+x^{j+1})$; these agree by Euler's identity $\prod_{n\ge1}(1+x^n)=\prod_{n\ge1}\frac1{1-x^{2n-1}}$.

questions.prompt: Let $a,b,c$ be elements of finite order in some group. Prove that if $a^{-1}ba=b^2$, $b^{-2}cb^2=c^2$ and $c^{-3}ac^3=a^2$, then $a=b=c=e$, where $e$ is the unit element.
questions.answer: Take the smallest prime $p$ dividing $\operatorname{ord}(a)\operatorname{ord}(b)\operatorname{ord}(c)$ and an element $d$ of order $p$ in the corresponding cyclic group; the conjugating element $g$ satisfies $g^{-1}dg=d^2$, so $g^{p-1}$ commutes with $d$, and since $\gcd(\operatorname{ord}g,p-1)=1$, $g$ itself commutes with $d$, forcing $d^2=d$.

questions.prompt:
Let $n>k$ and let $A_1,\ldots,A_k$ be real $n\times n$ matrices of rank $n-1$. Prove that
$$A_1\cdot\ldots\cdot A_k\neq0 .$$
questions.answer: Kernels add up at most: $\dim\ker(AB)\le\dim\ker A+\dim\ker B$, so $\dim\ker(A_1\cdots A_k)\le k<n$ and the product has rank $\ge n-k\ge1$.

questions.prompt:
Let $k$ be a positive integer. Compute
$$\sum_{n_1=1}^\infty\sum_{n_2=1}^\infty\cdots\sum_{n_k=1}^\infty\frac{1}{n_1n_2\cdots n_k\,(n_1+\cdots+n_k+1)} .$$
questions.answer: $k!$ (write $\frac1{N+1}=\int_0^1x^N\,dx$; the sum becomes $\int_0^1(-\ln(1-x))^k\,dx=\Gamma(k+1)$).

questions.prompt:
Let $p$ and $q$ be complex polynomials with $\deg p>\deg q$ and let $f(z)=\dfrac{p(z)}{q(z)}$. Suppose that all roots of $p$ lie inside the unit circle $|z|=1$ and that all roots of $q$ lie outside the unit circle. Prove that
$$\max_{|z|=1}|f'(z)|>\frac{\deg p-\deg q}{2}\max_{|z|=1}|f(z)| .$$
questions.answer: At a point $z_0$ of the unit circle where $|f|$ is maximal, $\left|\frac{z_0f'(z_0)}{f(z_0)}\right|\ge\operatorname{Re}\sum_k\frac{z_0}{z_0-c_k}-\operatorname{Re}\sum_l\frac{z_0}{z_0-d_l}>\frac{n_1}2-\frac{n_2}2$, because $\operatorname{Re}\frac1{1-w}>\frac12\iff|w|<1$.

questions.prompt:
Let $\mathbb Q[x]$ denote the vector space over $\mathbb Q$ of polynomials with rational coefficients in one variable $x$. Find all $\mathbb Q$-linear maps $\Phi:\mathbb Q[x]\to\mathbb Q[x]$ such that for any irreducible polynomial $p\in\mathbb Q[x]$ the polynomial $\Phi(p)$ is also irreducible.

(A polynomial $p\in\mathbb Q[x]$ is called irreducible if it is non-constant and the equality $p=q_1q_2$ is impossible for non-constant polynomials $q_1,q_2\in\mathbb Q[x]$.)
questions.answer: Exactly the maps $\Phi(p)(x)=a\,p(bx+c)$ with $a,b,c\in\mathbb Q$, $a,b\ne0$. (Show $\Phi(1)$ is a nonzero constant and $\Phi(x)$ linear, normalise to $\Phi(1)=1$, $\Phi(x)=x$, then prove $\Phi(x^n)=x^n$ by induction using Eisenstein polynomials with a prescribed value.)

questions.prompt: Let $f:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ be a differentiable function such that $|f'(x)|\neq1$ for all $x\in[0,1]$. Prove that there exist unique points $\alpha,\beta\in[0,1]$ such that $f(\alpha)=\alpha$ and $f(\beta)=1-\beta$.
questions.answer: Existence by the intermediate value theorem for $f(x)-x$ and $f(x)-(1-x)$; uniqueness because two solutions would give, by the mean value theorem, a point with $f'=1$ (resp. $f'=-1$).

questions.prompt:
Determine all $2\times2$ integer matrices $A$ having the following properties:

1. the entries of $A$ are (positive) prime numbers,
2. there exists a $2\times2$ integer matrix $B$ such that $A=B^2$ and the determinant of $B$ is the square of a prime number.
questions.answer: $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&11\\11&101\end{pmatrix}$ and $A=\begin{pmatrix}101&11\\11&2\end{pmatrix}$ (squares of $\pm\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&10\end{pmatrix}$ and $\pm\begin{pmatrix}10&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$).

questions.prompt:
Determine the smallest real number $C$ such that the inequality
$$\frac{x}{\sqrt{yz}}\cdot\frac{1}{x+1}+\frac{y}{\sqrt{zx}}\cdot\frac{1}{y+1}+\frac{z}{\sqrt{xy}}\cdot\frac{1}{z+1}\le C$$
holds for all positive real numbers $x$, $y$ and $z$ with
$$\frac{1}{x+1}+\frac{1}{y+1}+\frac{1}{z+1}=1 .$$
questions.answer: sqrt(2)

questions.prompt: Find all positive integers $n$ for which there exists a positive integer $k$ such that the decimal representation of $n^k$ starts and ends with the same digit.
questions.answer: Exactly the $n$ **not divisible by 10**. For $10\mid n$, $n^k$ ends in $0$; otherwise $n^{4m+1}$ always ends in the last digit $c$ of $n$, and the leading digits of $n^{4m+1}$ take every value, in particular $c$ (density of $\{m\cdot4\log_{10}n\}$).

questions.prompt:
Let $f:[1,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be a non-increasing function such that
$$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{f(2^{n+1})}{f(2^n)}<\frac12 .$$
Prove that
$$\int_1^\infty f(x)\,dx<\infty .$$
questions.answer: On $[2^n,2^{n+1}]$, $\int f\le2^nf(2^n)$, and $\sum 2^nf(2^n)$ converges by the ratio test because $\limsup\frac{2^{n+1}f(2^{n+1})}{2^nf(2^n)}<1$.

questions.prompt:
Let $M$ be the (tridiagonal) $10\times10$ matrix
$$M=\begin{pmatrix}
-1&3&0&0&\cdots&0&0\\
3&2&-1&0&\cdots&0&0\\
0&-1&2&-1&\cdots&0&0\\
\vdots&&\ddots&\ddots&\ddots&&\vdots\\
0&0&\cdots&-1&2&-1&0\\
0&0&\cdots&0&-1&2&-1\\
0&0&\cdots&0&0&-1&2
\end{pmatrix}$$
(that is, $m_{11}=-1$, $m_{12}=m_{21}=3$, $m_{ii}=2$ for $2\le i\le10$, $m_{i,i+1}=m_{i+1,i}=-1$ for $2\le i\le9$, and all other entries $0$). Show that $M$ has exactly nine positive real eigenvalues (counted with multiplicities).
questions.answer: $M$ is symmetric; on the 9-dimensional subspace $\{x_1=0\}$ the form $x^TMx=x_2^2+\sum(x_{i+1}-x_i)^2+x_{10}^2$ is positive definite, while $y=(1,-1,0,\dots,0)$ gives $y^TMy=-5<0$; a dimension count then gives exactly one negative and nine positive eigenvalues.

questions.prompt: Let $(A,+,\cdot)$ be a ring with unity, having the following property: for all $x\in A$ either $x^2=1$ or $x^n=0$ for some $n\in\mathbb N$. Show that $A$ is a commutative ring.
questions.answer: Units satisfy $x^2=1$, so the unit group is commutative ($(xy)^2=1\Rightarrow xy=yx$); non-units are nilpotent, so $1-x$ is a unit for every non-unit $x$; then $xy=yx$ follows by replacing non-units $x$ by the units $1-x$.

questions.prompt:
Let $a,b,c,x,y,z,t$ be positive real numbers with $1\le x,y,z\le4$. Prove that
$$\frac{x}{(2a)^t}+\frac{y}{(2b)^t}+\frac{z}{(2c)^t}\ \ge\ \frac{y+z-x}{(b+c)^t}+\frac{z+x-y}{(c+a)^t}+\frac{x+y-z}{(a+b)^t} .$$
questions.answer: A weighted Schur inequality $x(A-B)(A-C)+y(B-A)(B-C)+z(C-A)(C-B)\ge0$ (valid for weights in $[1,4]$), applied to $A=e^{-as},B=e^{-bs},C=e^{-cs}$ and integrated against $s^{t-1}ds$, using $\int_0^\infty s^{t-1}e^{-ps}ds=\Gamma(t)p^{-t}$.

questions.prompt: Let $f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be a differentiable function with $|f(x)|\le M$ and $f(x)f'(x)\ge\cos x$ for $x\in[0,\infty)$, where $M>0$. Prove that $f(x)$ does not have a limit as $x\to\infty$.
questions.answer: $F(x)=f(x)^2-2\sin x$ is non-decreasing ($F'=2ff'-2\cos x\ge0$) and bounded, so it has a limit; if $f$ had a limit, $2\sin x=f^2-F$ would too — impossible.

questions.prompt: Let $A=(a_{ij})$ and $B=(b_{ij})$ be two real $10\times10$ matrices such that $a_{ij}=b_{ij}+1$ for all $i,j$ and $A^3=0$. Prove that $\det B=0$.
questions.answer: $B=A-H$ with $H$ the all-ones matrix (rank 1); expanding $(A-H)^3$, all terms except $A^3=0$ contain $H$ and have rank $\le1$, so $\operatorname{rank}B^3\le7<10$.

questions.prompt: Let $S$ be a finite set of integers. Prove that there exists a number $c$ depending on $S$ such that for each non-constant polynomial $f$ with integer coefficients the number of integers $k$ satisfying $f(k)\in S$ does not exceed $\max(\deg f,c)$.
questions.answer: $c=4d$ with $d=\max S-\min S$: if $f$ hits only one value of $S$ there are $\le\deg f$ solutions; if it hits $s_1\ne s_2$ at $k_1,k_2$, then $(k-k_1)\mid(f(k)-s_1)$ bounds all other solutions to $|k-k_1|\le d$ or $|k-k_2|\le d$.

questions.prompt:
Let $n$ and $k$ be positive integers. Evaluate the following sum
$$\sum_{j=0}^{k}\binom{k}{j}^{2}\binom{n+2k-j}{2k},$$
where $\binom nk=\dfrac{n!}{k!\,(n-k)!}$.
questions.answer: $\dbinom{n+k}{k}^{2}$ (Li Shanlan's identity; reduce to $\sum_j\binom kj\binom nj\binom{n+2k-j}{k-j}=\binom{n+k}k\binom{2k}k$ and apply Vandermonde twice).

questions.prompt: Let $S_n$ denote the sum of the first $n$ prime numbers. Prove that for any $n$ there exists the square of an integer between $S_n$ and $S_{n+1}$.
questions.answer: It suffices that $\sqrt{S_{n+1}}-\sqrt{S_n}>1$, i.e. $p_{n+1}>1+2\sqrt{S_n}$; for $n\ge5$, $S_n<1+3+5+\dots+p_n=\frac{(p_n+1)^2}4$ gives $2\sqrt{S_n}<p_n+1\le p_{n+1}-1$; check $n\le4$ by hand.

questions.prompt: An $n$-dimensional cube is given. Consider all the segments connecting any two different vertices of the cube. How many distinct intersection points do these segments have (excluding the vertices)?
questions.answer: $3^n-2^n-n\,2^{n-1}$: the intersection points are exactly the points with all coordinates in $\{0,\tfrac12,1\}$ and at least two coordinates equal to $\tfrac12$.

questions.prompt: Prove that there is no polynomial $P$ with integer coefficients such that $P\left(\sqrt[3]5+\sqrt[3]{25}\right)=5+\sqrt[3]5$.
questions.answer: $x_0=\sqrt[3]5+\sqrt[3]{25}$ is a root of the monic $Q(x)=x^3-15x-30$; reducing $P$ mod $Q$ gives an integer polynomial $w$ of degree $\le2$ with $w(x_0)=5+\sqrt[3]5$, but the only rational such $w$ is $\frac14x^2-\frac14x+\frac52$.

questions.prompt:
Let $\mathcal F$ be the set of all continuous functions $f:[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ with the property
$$\left|\int_0^x\frac{f(t)}{\sqrt{x-t}}\,dt\right|\le1\qquad\text{for all }x\in(0,1] .$$
Compute $\displaystyle\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\left|\int_0^1f(x)\,dx\right|$.
questions.answer: 2/pi

questions.prompt: Find all complex numbers $z$ such that $\left|z^3+2-2i\right|+z\bar z|z|=2\sqrt2$. ($\bar z$ is the conjugate of $z$.)
questions.answer: $z=\varrho\,e^{i(\pi/4+2k\pi/3)}$ with $0\le\varrho\le\sqrt2$ and $k\in\{0,1,2\}$: three segments from $0$ to $1+i$, $(1+i)e^{2\pi i/3}$, $(1+i)e^{4\pi i/3}$ (equality case of the triangle inequality: $z^3\in[0,-2+2i]$).

questions.prompt: We have a deck of $2n$ cards. Each shuffling changes the order from $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n,b_1,b_2,\ldots,b_n$ to $a_1,b_1,a_2,b_2,\ldots,a_n,b_n$. Determine all even numbers $2n$ such that after shuffling the deck $8$ times the original order is restored.
questions.answer: $2n\in\{2,4,6,16,18,52,86,256\}$, i.e. exactly when $2n-1\mid 2^8-1=255$ (the shuffle acts on positions $0,\dots,2n-2$ as $k\mapsto2k\bmod(2n-1)$).

questions.prompt:
Let $n\ge2$ be an integer and let $x>0$ be a real number. Prove that
$$\left(1-\sqrt{\tanh x}\right)^n+\sqrt{\tanh(nx)}<1 .$$
Recall that $\tanh t=\dfrac{e^{2t}-1}{e^{2t}+1}$.
questions.answer: With $g(t)=1-\sqrt{\tanh t}$ prove $g(x)g(y)<g(x+y)$ for $x,y>0$ (via $\tanh(x+y)=\frac{\tanh x+\tanh y}{1+\tanh x\tanh y}$ and an algebraic inequality in $u=\sqrt{\tanh x}$, $v=\sqrt{\tanh y}$), then induct: $g(x)^n<g(nx)$.

questions.prompt: Let $P_1,P_2,P_3,P_4$ be the graphs of four quadratic polynomials drawn in the coordinate plane. Suppose that $P_1$ is tangent to $P_2$ at the point $q_2$, $P_2$ is tangent to $P_3$ at the point $q_3$, $P_3$ is tangent to $P_4$ at the point $q_4$, and $P_4$ is tangent to $P_1$ at the point $q_1$. Assume that all the points $q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4$ have distinct $x$-coordinates. Prove that $q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4$ lie on a graph of an at most quadratic polynomial.
questions.answer: Tangency means $f_1-f_2=c_2(x-x_2)^2$, etc.; summing gives $\sum c_i(x-x_i)^2\equiv0$, hence $\sum c_i(x_3-x_i)(x_4-x_i)=0$, which is exactly the consistency condition for the curve $y=f_1(x)+k(x-x_1)(x-x_2)$ to pass through $q_3$ and $q_4$.

questions.prompt:
Let $f:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be a differentiable function. Assume that
$$\lim_{x\to\infty}\left(f(x)+\frac{f'(x)}{x}\right)=0 .$$
Prove that
$$\lim_{x\to\infty}f(x)=0 .$$
questions.answer: Apply Cauchy's mean value theorem to $g(x)=e^{x^2/2}f(x)$ and $h(x)=e^{x^2/2}$: $\frac{g'}{h'}=f+\frac{f'}{x}$, which gives $|f(x)|\le|f(x_0)|e^{(x_0^2-x^2)/2}+\varepsilon$.

questions.prompt: Let $p$ be a prime number and let $A$ be a subgroup of the multiplicative group $\mathbb F_p^*$ of the finite field $\mathbb F_p$ with $p$ elements. Prove that if the order of $A$ is a multiple of $6$, then there exist $x,y,z\in A$ satisfying $x+y=z$.
questions.answer: $A$ is cyclic, so it contains an element $a$ of order $6$; then $a^3=-1$ and $a^2-a+1=0$, so $x=a^2$, $y=1$, $z=a$ works.

questions.prompt:
Let $k$ be a positive even integer. Show that
$$\sum_{n=0}^{k/2}(-1)^n\binom{k+2}{n}\binom{2(k-n)+1}{k+1}=\frac{(k+1)(k+2)}{2} .$$
questions.answer: Compare the coefficients of $x^k$ in $(1-x)^{k+2}=(1-x^2)^{k+2}(1+x)^{-(k+2)}$, using $[x^m](1+x)^{-N}=(-1)^m\binom{N+m-1}{N-1}$.

questions.prompt:
Let $0<a<b$ and let $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous function with $\int_a^bf(t)\,dt=0$. Show that
$$\int_a^b\!\!\int_a^bf(x)f(y)\ln(x+y)\,dx\,dy\le0 .$$
questions.answer: Frullani: $\ln s=\int_0^\infty\frac{e^{-t}-e^{-st}}{t}\,dt$; by Fubini and $\int f=0$ the double integral equals $-\int_0^\infty\frac{F(t)^2}{t}\,dt\le0$ with $F(t)=\int_a^bf(x)e^{-xt}\,dx$.

questions.prompt:
Let $f\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be differentiable on $\mathbb R$. Prove that there exists $x\in[0,1]$ such that
$$\frac{4}{\pi}\big(f(1)-f(0)\big)=(1+x^2)f'(x).$$
questions.answer: Apply the mean value theorem to $\psi(t)=f(\tan t)$ on $[0,\pi/4]$ (or Cauchy's mean value theorem to $f$ and $\arctan$).

questions.prompt: Consider the infinite chessboard whose rows and columns are indexed by positive integers. Is it possible to put a single positive rational number into each cell of the chessboard so that each positive rational number appears exactly once and the sum of every row and of every column is finite?
questions.answer: Yes

questions.prompt: Let $P(x)=x^{2015}-2x^{2014}+1$ and $Q(x)=x^{2015}-2x^{2014}-1$. Determine for each of the polynomials $P$ and $Q$ whether it is a divisor of some nonzero polynomial $c_0+c_1x+\dots+c_nx^n$ whose coefficients $c_i$ are all in the set $\{1,-1\}$.
questions.answer: P: yes, Q: no

questions.prompt:
Let $m$ be a positive integer and let $p$ be a prime divisor of $m$. Suppose that the complex polynomial $a_0+a_1x+\dots+a_nx^n$ with $n<\frac{p}{p-1}\varphi(m)$ and $a_n\ne0$ is divisible by the cyclotomic polynomial $\Phi_m(x)$. Prove that there are at least $p$ nonzero coefficients $a_i$.

The cyclotomic polynomial $\Phi_m(x)$ is the monic polynomial whose roots are the $m$-th primitive complex roots of unity. Euler's totient function $\varphi(m)$ denotes the number of positive integers less than or equal to $m$ which are coprime to $m$.
questions.answer: Induct on the exponent of $p$ in $m$. If $p\,\|\,m$, one shows that every residue class modulo $p$ contains an index $\ell$ with $a_\ell\ne0$ (use a root $w$ of $\Phi_k(x^p)$ with $f(w)\ne0$ and a roots-of-unity filter). If $p^2\mid m$, split $f$ by exponents modulo $p$ and reduce to $m/p$.

questions.prompt:
Let $A$ and $B$ be two $3\times3$ matrices with real entries. Prove that
$$A-\left(A^{-1}+\left(B^{-1}-A\right)^{-1}\right)^{-1}=ABA,$$
provided all the inverses appearing on the left-hand side of the equality exist.

Determine all pairs $(n,m)$ of positive integers satisfying the equation
$$5^n=6m^2+1 .$$

Determine the set of real values of $x$ for which the following series converges, and find its sum:
$$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left(\sum_{\substack{k_1,\dots,k_n\ge0\\ 1\cdot k_1+2\cdot k_2+\dots+n\cdot k_n=n}}\frac{(k_1+\dots+k_n)!}{k_1!\cdots k_n!}\,x^{k_1+\dots+k_n}\right).$$
questions.answer: The inner sum equals $x(1+x)^{n-1}$. The series converges exactly for $-2<x\le0$, with sum $-1$ for $-2<x<0$ and $0$ for $x=0$.

questions.prompt:
Find all continuously differentiable functions $f\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, such that for every $a\ge0$ the following relation holds:
