$$\iiint\limits_{D(a)}x\,f\!\left(\frac{ay}{\sqrt{x^2+y^2}}\right)dx\,dy\,dz=\frac{\pi a^3}{8}\big(f(a)+\sin a-1\big),$$
where $D(a)=\left\{(x,y,z):x^2+y^2+z^2\le a^2,\ |y|\le\frac{x}{\sqrt3}\right\}$.
questions.answer: Exactly the functions with $f|_{[0,\infty)}\in C^2[0,\infty)$, $f(0)=1$, $f'(0)=f''(0)=0$ (one-sided), extended by $f(-t)=2f'(2t)+2\cos 2t-f(t)$ for $t>0$. The condition is equivalent to $\int_{-a/2}^{a/2}f=f(a)+\sin a-1$. Example: $f=1$ on $[0,\infty)$, $f(x)=2\cos 2x-1$ for $x<0$.

questions.prompt:
Let $f\colon\mathbb R\to(0,\infty)$ be a continuously differentiable function. Prove that there exists $\xi\in(0,1)$ such that
$$e^{f'(\xi)}f(0)^{f(\xi)}=f(1)^{f(\xi)} .$$
questions.answer: Taking logarithms, the equality is $\frac{f'(\xi)}{f(\xi)}=\ln f(1)-\ln f(0)$: the mean value theorem for $\ln f$ on $[0,1]$.

questions.prompt:
Find all positive integers $n$ such that $\varphi(n)$ divides $n^2+3$.

($\varphi(n)$ denotes Euler's totient function, i.e. the number of positive integers $k\le n$ coprime to $n$.)

Let $d\ge3$ and let $A_1\dots A_{d+1}$ be a simplex in $\mathbb R^d$. (A simplex is the convex hull of $d+1$ points not lying in a common hyperplane.) For every $i=1,\dots,d+1$ let $O_i$ be the circumcentre of the face $A_1\dots A_{i-1}A_{i+1}\dots A_{d+1}$, i.e. $O_i$ lies in the hyperplane $A_1\dots A_{i-1}A_{i+1}\dots A_{d+1}$ and it has the same distance from all points $A_1,\dots,A_{i-1},A_{i+1},\dots,A_{d+1}$. For each $i$ draw a line through $A_i$ perpendicular to the hyperplane $O_1\dots O_{i-1}O_{i+1}\dots O_{d+1}$. Prove that either these lines are parallel or they have a common point.
questions.answer: If the $O_i$ span only a hyperplane, the lines are parallel. Otherwise they all pass through $P=2Q-O$, where $O$ and $Q$ are the circumcentres of the $A_i$ and of the $O_i$: each $O_j$ ($j\ne i$) lies on the sphere with diameter $OA_i$.

questions.prompt:
Find the value of the sum $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^\infty A_n$, where
$$A_n=\sum_{k_1=1}^\infty\cdots\sum_{k_n=1}^\infty\frac1{k_1^2}\,\frac1{k_1^2+k_2^2}\cdots\frac1{k_1^2+\dots+k_n^2}.$$

Let $a,b$ and $c$ be positive real numbers such that $a+b+c=1$. Show that
$$\left(\frac1a+\frac1{bc}\right)\left(\frac1b+\frac1{ca}\right)\left(\frac1c+\frac1{ab}\right)\ge1728 .$$
questions.answer: $\frac1a+\frac1{bc}=\frac{(a+b)(a+c)}{abc}$, so the product is $\frac{[(a+b)(b+c)(c+a)]^2}{(abc)^3}\ge\frac{64}{abc}\ge64\cdot27=1728$. Equality holds at $a=b=c=\frac13$.

questions.prompt: Let $X$ be a set and let $\mathcal P(X)$ be the set of all subsets of $X$. Let $\mu\colon\mathcal P(X)\to\mathcal P(X)$ be a map with the property that $\mu(A\cup B)=\mu(A)\cup\mu(B)$ whenever $A$ and $B$ are disjoint subsets of $X$. Prove that there exists a set $F\subset X$ such that $\mu(F)=F$.
questions.answer: $\mu$ is monotone. Then $F=\bigcap\{A:\mu(A)\subset A\}$ is a fixed point (Knaster–Tarski).

questions.prompt:
For $n\ge3$ find the eigenvalues (with their multiplicities) of the $n\times n$ matrix
$$\begin{bmatrix}1&0&1&0&0&0&\cdots&\cdots&0&0\\0&2&0&1&0&0&\cdots&\cdots&0&0\\1&0&2&0&1&0&\cdots&\cdots&0&0\\0&1&0&2&0&1&\cdots&\cdots&0&0\\0&0&1&0&2&0&\cdots&\cdots&0&0\\0&0&0&1&0&2&\cdots&\cdots&0&0\\\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\ddots&&\vdots&\vdots\\\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&&\ddots&\vdots&\vdots\\0&0&0&0&0&0&\cdots&\cdots&2&0\\0&0&0&0&0&0&\cdots&\cdots&0&1\end{bmatrix}.$$
questions.answer: $4\cos^2\frac{k\pi}{n+1}$ for $k=1,\dots,n$. For $1\le k\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ these are distinct and each has multiplicity $2$; for odd $n$ there is in addition the simple eigenvalue $0$ (from $k=\frac{n+1}2$). The matrix is $B^2$ with $B$ the path adjacency matrix.

questions.prompt:
Let $f\colon[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be a continuously differentiable function satisfying
$$f(x)=\int_{x-1}^xf(t)\,dt$$
for all $x\ge1$. Show that $f$ has bounded variation on $[1,\infty)$, i.e.
$$\int_1^\infty|f'(x)|\,dx<\infty .$$
questions.answer: For $x\ge1$, $g=f'$ satisfies $g(x)=\int_{x-1}^xg$ and $\int_{x-1}^x(t-x+1)g(t)\,dt=0$. Hence $|g(x)|\le\frac12\max_{[x-1,x]}|g|$, the maxima of $|f'|$ on $[n,n+1]$ decay geometrically, and $\int_1^\infty|f'|<\infty$.

questions.prompt:
Let $f\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous function satisfying
$$f(x+2y)=2f(x)f(y)$$
for every $x,y\in\mathbb R$. Prove that $f$ is constant.
questions.answer: $y=0$ gives $f\equiv0$ or $f(0)=\frac12$. In the second case $x=0$ gives $f(2y)=f(y)$, so $f(a)=f(a/2^n)\to f(0)=\frac12$.

questions.prompt:
We say that we extend a finite sequence of positive integers $(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ if we replace it by
$$(1,2,\dots,a_1-1,a_1,1,2,\dots,a_2-1,a_2,1,2,\dots,a_3-1,a_3,\dots,1,2,\dots,a_n-1,a_n),$$
i.e., each element $k$ of the original sequence is replaced by $1,2,\dots,k-1,k$. Géza takes the sequence $(1,2,\dots,9)$ and he extends it $2017$ times. Then he chooses randomly one element of the resulting sequence. What is the probability that the chosen element is $1$?

Let $P$ be a convex polyhedron. Jaroslav writes a non-negative real number to every vertex of $P$ in such a way that the sum of these numbers is $1$. Afterwards, to every edge he writes the product of the numbers at the two endpoints of that edge. Prove that the sum of the numbers at the edges is at most $\frac38$.
questions.answer: Some maximizer is supported on a clique of the (planar) edge graph, hence on at most $4$ vertices, and $\sum_{i<j\le4}a_ia_j\le\frac38$ when $\sum a_i=1$.

questions.prompt:
Let $f\colon(1,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be a continuously differentiable function satisfying $f(x)\le x^2\log(x)$ and $f'(x)>0$ for every $x\in(1,\infty)$. Prove that
$$\int_1^\infty\frac1{f'(x)}\,dx=\infty .$$
questions.answer: Cauchy–Schwarz: $\big(\int_e^a\frac1{f'}\big)\big(\int_e^a\frac{f'}{(x\log x)^2}\big)\ge(\log\log a)^2$. Integration by parts with $f\le x^2\log x$ gives $\int_e^a\frac{f'}{(x\log x)^2}\le2\log\log a+C$.

questions.prompt:
Let $(a_n)_{n=1}^\infty$ be a sequence with $a_n\in\{0,1\}$ for every $n$. Let $F\colon(-1,1)\to\mathbb R$ be defined by
$$F(x)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_nx^n$$
and assume that $F\left(\frac12\right)$ is rational. Show that $F$ is the quotient of two polynomials with integer coefficients.
questions.answer: $F(\frac12)$ is a rational number with binary digits $a_n$, so $(a_n)$ is eventually periodic; then $F(x)=A(x)+\frac{B(x)}{1-x^p}$ with integer polynomials $A,B$.

questions.prompt: Prove or disprove the following statement. If $g\colon(0,1)\to(0,1)$ is an increasing function and satisfies $g(x)>x$ for all $x\in(0,1)$, then there exists a continuous function $f\colon(0,1)\to\mathbb R$ satisfying $f(x)<f(g(x))$ for all $x\in(0,1)$, but $f$ is not an increasing function.
questions.answer: True

questions.prompt:
Let $n\ge2$ be an integer. Consider the system of equations
$$x_1+\frac2{x_2}=x_2+\frac2{x_3}=\dots=x_n+\frac2{x_1}.\tag{1}$$
1. Prove that (1) has infinitely many real solutions $(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ such that the numbers $x_1,\dots,x_n$ are distinct.
2. Prove that every solution $(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ of (1), such that the numbers $x_1,\dots,x_n$ are not all equal, satisfies $|x_1x_2\cdots x_n|=2^{n/2}$.
questions.answer: (2) Telescoping differences: $x_2-x_1=\frac{2}{x_2x_3}(x_3-x_2)=\dots$, so $(x_1\cdots x_n)^2=2^n$. (1) With common value $A=2\sqrt2\cos\frac\pi n$, the Möbius map $x\mapsto A-\frac2x$ (matrix $\begin{pmatrix}A&-2\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ with eigenvalues $\sqrt2e^{\pm i\pi/n}$) has $n$-th iterate equal to the identity, which gives infinitely many solutions with distinct entries.

questions.prompt: A positive integer $t$ is called a Jane's integer if $t=x^3+y^2$ for some positive integers $x$ and $y$. Prove that for every integer $n\ge2$ there exist infinitely many positive integers $m$ such that the set of $n^2$ consecutive integers $\{m+1,m+2,\dots,m+n^2\}$ contains exactly $n+1$ Jane's integers.
questions.answer: The count $C(m)$ of Jane's integers in the window changes by at most $1$ when $m$ increases by $1$. Windows with $C=0$ exist arbitrarily far out (there are only about $u^5$ Jane's integers up to $u^6$), and windows with $C\ge n+1$ exist arbitrarily far out ($i^6+j^2$ and $8+i^6$; for $n=2$ use a Pell equation). A discrete intermediate value argument finishes.

questions.prompt: Every point of the rectangle $R=[0,4]\times[0,40]$ is coloured using one of four colours. Show that there exist four points in $R$ with the same colour that form a rectangle having integer side lengths.
questions.answer: Pigeonhole on the $41$ rows $\{(k,j):k=0,\dots,4\}$, $j=0,\dots,40$. Each row has a monochromatic pair; there are only $4\cdot\binom52=40$ possible (colour, pair) types, so two rows share one.

questions.prompt:
Find all prime numbers $p$ such that $p^3$ divides the determinant
$$\begin{vmatrix}2^2&1&1&\cdots&1\\1&3^2&1&\cdots&1\\1&1&4^2&&1\\\vdots&\vdots&&\ddots&\\1&1&1&&(p+7)^2\end{vmatrix}.$$
questions.answer: $p\in\{2,3,5,181\}$. With $n=p+6$, the determinant equals $\frac{7n^2+17n+8}{8}(n!)^2$.

questions.prompt:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $x_1,\dots,x_n$ be positive real numbers satisfying $|x_i-x_j|\le1$ for all pairs $(i,j)$ with $1\le i<j\le n$. Prove that
$$\frac{x_1}{x_2}+\frac{x_2}{x_3}+\dots+\frac{x_{n-1}}{x_n}+\frac{x_n}{x_1}\ge\frac{x_2+1}{x_1+1}+\frac{x_3+1}{x_2+1}+\dots+\frac{x_n+1}{x_{n-1}+1}+\frac{x_1+1}{x_n+1}.$$
questions.answer: With $h(t)=t-\ln t$, show $h\big(\frac xy\big)\ge h\big(\frac{y+1}{x+1}\big)$ whenever $|x-y|\le1$, and sum cyclically; the logarithms telescope to $0$.

questions.prompt:
Determine all possible (finite or infinite) values of
$$\lim_{x\to-\infty}f(x)-\lim_{x\to+\infty}f(x),$$
if $f\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is a strictly decreasing continuous function satisfying
$$f(f(x))^4-f(f(x))+f(x)=1$$
for all $x\in\mathbb R$.
questions.answer: Exactly the numbers in the open interval $\big(0,(1+z)^4-1\big)$, where $z=\frac{3}{4\sqrt[3]4}$ (so $(1+z)^4-1\approx3.701$); infinite values are impossible.

questions.prompt:
Find all real solutions of the equation
$$17^x+2^x=11^x+2^{3x}.$$

Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $a_1\le a_2\le\dots\le a_n$ be real numbers such that
$$a_1+2a_2+\dots+na_n=0 .$$
Prove that
$$a_1[x]+a_2[2x]+\dots+a_n[nx]\ge0$$
for every real number $x$. (Here $[t]$ denotes the integer satisfying $[t]\le t<[t]+1$.)
questions.answer: Key fact: $[ix]+[(k-i)x]\le[kx]$. Either induct on $n$ by spreading $a_{n+1}$ over the first $n$ terms, or use Abel summation with $P_k=\sum_{j\le k}[jx]$, for which $P_k/(k(k+1))$ is nondecreasing.

questions.prompt: In $\mathbb R^3$ some $n$ points are coloured. In every step, if four coloured points lie on the same line, Vojtěch can colour any other point on this line. He observes that he can colour any point $P\in\mathbb R^3$ in a finite number of steps (possibly depending on $P$). Find the minimal value of $n$ for which this could happen.

Compute the integral
$$\iint\limits_{\mathbb R^2}\left(\frac{1-e^{-xy}}{xy}\right)^2e^{-x^2-y^2}\,dx\,dy .$$

Let $\{a_n\}_{n=0}^\infty$ be a sequence given recursively by $a_0=1$ and
$$a_{n+1}=\frac{7a_n+\sqrt{45a_n^2-36}}{2},\qquad n=0,1,\dots$$
Show that the following statements hold for all positive integers $n$:

a) $a_n$ is a positive integer.

b) $a_na_{n+1}-1$ is the square of an integer.
questions.answer: Squaring $2a_{n+1}-7a_n=\sqrt{45a_n^2-36}$ gives $a_{n+1}^2-7a_na_{n+1}+a_n^2+9=0$; by Vieta $a_{n+1}=7a_n-a_{n-1}$ (so all terms are integers), and $(a_n+a_{n+1})^2=9(a_na_{n+1}-1)$.

questions.prompt:
A triplet of polynomials $u,v,w\in\mathbb R[x,y,z]$ is called *smart* if there exist polynomials $P,Q,R\in\mathbb R[x,y,z]$ such that the following polynomial identity holds:
$$u^{2019}P+v^{2019}Q+w^{2019}R=2019 .$$

a) Is the triplet of polynomials
$$u=x+2y+3,\qquad v=y+z+2,\qquad w=x+y+z$$
smart?

b) Is the triplet of polynomials
$$u=x+2y+3,\qquad v=y+z+2,\qquad w=x+y-z$$
smart?

(Answer both parts, e.g. "yes, no".)
questions.answer: No, yes

questions.prompt:
For an invertible $n\times n$ matrix $M$ with integer entries we define a sequence $\mathcal S_M=\{M_i\}_{i=0}^\infty$ by the recurrence
$$M_0=M,\qquad M_{i+1}=(M_i^T)^{-1}M_i,\quad i=0,1,\dots$$
Find the smallest integer $n\ge2$ for which there exists a normal $n\times n$ matrix $M$ with integer entries such that its sequence $\mathcal S_M$ is non-constant and has period $P=7$, i.e., $M_{i+7}=M_i$ for all $i=0,1,\dots$

($M^T$ means the transpose of a matrix $M$. A square matrix $M$ is called normal if $M^TM=MM^T$ holds.)

Determine the largest constant $K\ge0$ such that
$$\frac{a^a(b^2+c^2)}{(a^a-1)^2}+\frac{b^b(c^2+a^2)}{(b^b-1)^2}+\frac{c^c(a^2+b^2)}{(c^c-1)^2}\ge K\left(\frac{a+b+c}{abc-1}\right)^2$$
holds for all positive real numbers $a,b,c$ such that $ab+bc+ca=abc$.

a) Is it true that for every non-empty set $A$ and every associative operation $*\colon A\times A\to A$ the conditions
$$x*x*y=y\qquad\text{and}\qquad y*x*x=y\qquad\text{for every }x,y\in A$$
imply commutativity of $*$?

b) Is it true that for every non-empty set $A$ and every associative operation $*\colon A\times A\to A$ the condition
$$x*x*y=y\qquad\text{for every }x,y\in A$$
implies commutativity of $*$?

(Answer both parts, e.g. "yes, no".)
questions.answer: Yes, no

questions.prompt:
Find all twice differentiable functions $f\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ such that
$$f''(x)\cos(f(x))\ge(f'(x))^2\sin(f(x))\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R.$$
questions.answer: Only the constant functions: the condition says $g=\sin f$ satisfies $g''\ge0$, and a bounded convex function on $\mathbb R$ is constant, which forces $f$ to be constant.

questions.prompt:
Let $p$ be an even non-negative continuous function with $\int_{\mathbb R}p(x)\,dx=1$ and let $n$ be a positive integer. Let $\xi_1,\xi_2,\dots,\xi_n$ be independent identically distributed random variables with density function $p$. Define
$$X_0=0,\quad X_1=X_0+\xi_1,\quad X_2=X_1+\xi_2,\quad\dots,\quad X_n=X_{n-1}+\xi_n .$$
Prove that the probability that all the random variables $X_1,X_2,\dots,X_{n-1}$ lie between $X_0$ and $X_n$ equals $\frac1n$.
questions.answer: Write $\xi_1,\dots,\xi_n,-\xi_1,\dots,-\xi_n$ around a circle; the event for the $n$ cyclic shifts $(\xi_{m+1},\dots,\xi_n,-\xi_1,\dots,-\xi_m)$ happens for exactly one shift almost surely (where the closed walk attains its maximum or minimum), and all shifts have the same distribution because $p$ is even, so $n\cdot P=1$.

questions.prompt:
Let $D=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Im}z>0,\ \operatorname{Re}z>0\}$. Let $n\ge1$ and let $a_1,\dots,a_n\in D$ be distinct complex numbers. Define
$$f(z)=z\cdot\prod_{j=1}^n\frac{z-a_j}{z-\overline{a_j}} .$$
Prove that $f'$ has at least one root in $D$.
questions.answer: The $2n$ roots $b_k$ of $f'$ satisfy $\sum 1/b_k=2\sum1/a_j$, so some root lies in the upper half-plane; and $\operatorname{Re}\frac{f'}{f}<0$ on $\{\operatorname{Re}z\le0<\operatorname{Im}z\}$, so that root lies in $D$.

questions.prompt:
Assume that a real polynomial $P(x)$ has no real roots. Prove that the polynomial
$$Q(x)=P(x)+\frac{P''(x)}{2!}+\frac{P^{(4)}(x)}{4!}+\dots$$
also has no real roots.
questions.answer: By Taylor's formula $Q(x)=\frac{P(x+1)+P(x-1)}{2}$; $P$ has constant sign on $\mathbb R$, hence so does $Q$.

questions.prompt:
Let $n\ge1$. Assume that $A$ is a real $n\times n$ matrix which satisfies the equality
$$A^7+A^5+A^3+A-I=0 .$$
Show that $\det(A)>0$.
questions.answer: Every eigenvalue is a root of $w(x)=x^7+x^5+x^3+x-1$; $w$ is strictly increasing, so its only real root is positive, and non-real eigenvalues come in conjugate pairs, so $\det A=\lambda_0^{k}\prod|\lambda_j|^{2k_j}>0$.

questions.prompt:
Let $f\colon[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ be a given continuous function. Find the limit
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}(n+1)\sum_{k=0}^n\int_0^1x^k(1-x)^{n-k}f(x)\,dx .$$
questions.answer: The limit is $f(0)+f(1)$: the kernel $K_n(x)=(n+1)\sum_k x^k(1-x)^{n-k}$ is symmetric, has total integral $\sum_k\binom nk^{-1}\to2$, and tends to $0$ uniformly away from the endpoints.

questions.prompt:
In a box there are $31$, $41$ and $59$ stones coloured, respectively, red, green and blue. Three players, having t-shirts of these three colours, play the following game. They sequentially make one of two moves:

(I) either remove three stones of one colour from the box,

(II) or replace two stones of different colours by two stones of the third colour.

The game ends when all the stones in the box have the same colour and the winner is the player whose t-shirt has this colour. Assuming that the players play optimally, is it possible to decide whether the game ends and who will win, depending on who the starting player is?
questions.answer: Yes. Invariants mod 3 show that the game can only end with red stones, so Red wins if it ends. If Red starts, Green and Blue can keep the game going forever (it never ends); if Green or Blue starts, Red wins.

questions.prompt:
Determine whether there exists a differentiable function $f\colon[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ such that
$$f(0)=f(1)=1,\qquad|f'(x)|\le2\ \text{for all }x\in[0,1]\qquad\text{and}\qquad\left|\int_0^1f(x)\,dx\right|\le\frac12 .$$
questions.answer: No

questions.prompt: For any given pair of positive integers $m>n$ find all $a\in\mathbb R$ for which the polynomial $x^m-ax^n+1$ can be expressed as a quotient of two nonzero polynomials with real nonnegative coefficients.
questions.answer: Exactly the $a$ with $a<m\,n^{-n/m}(m-n)^{n/m-1}=\dfrac{m}{n^{n/m}(m-n)^{(m-n)/m}}$, i.e. exactly when $x^m-ax^n+1$ has no positive root.

questions.prompt:
Let $x_1,\dots,x_n$ be given real numbers with $0<m\le x_i\le M$ for each $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$. Let $X$ be the discrete random variable uniformly distributed on $\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}$. The mean $\mu$ and the variance $\sigma^2$ of $X$ are defined as
$$\mu(X)=\frac{x_1+\dots+x_n}{n}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\sigma^2(X)=\frac{(x_1-\mu(X))^2+\dots+(x_n-\mu(X))^2}{n}.$$
By $X^2$ denote the discrete random variable uniformly distributed on $\{x_1^2,\dots,x_n^2\}$. Prove that
$$\sigma^2(X)\ge\left(\frac{m}{2M^2}\right)^2\sigma^2(X^2).$$
questions.answer: In fact $\sigma^2(X^2)\le4M^2\sigma^2(X)$, because $(x_i^2-x_j^2)^2=(x_i+x_j)^2(x_i-x_j)^2\le4M^2(x_i-x_j)^2$; and $\frac{m^2}{4M^4}\cdot4M^2=\frac{m^2}{M^2}\le1$.

questions.prompt:
A function $f\colon\mathbb Z^+\to\mathbb R$ is called multiplicative if for every $a,b\in\mathbb Z^+$ with $\gcd(a,b)=1$ we have $f(ab)=f(a)f(b)$. Let $g$ be the multiplicative function given by
$$g(p^\alpha)=\alpha p^{\alpha-1},$$
where $\alpha\in\mathbb Z^+$ and $p>0$ is a prime. Prove that there exist infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that
$$g(n)+1=g(n+1).$$
questions.answer: $g(13^2)=26$, $g(3^3)=27$ and $g=1$ on squarefree numbers; take $n=169x$, $n+1=27y$ with $x=77+1053t$, $y=482+6591t$ squarefree, which happens for a positive proportion of $t$ (e.g. $n=13013$).

questions.prompt:
Let $f\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be a continuously differentiable function. Prove that
$$\left|f(1)-\int_0^1f(x)\,dx\right|\le\frac12\max_{x\in[0,1]}|f'(x)| .$$
questions.answer: $f(1)-\int_0^1f=\int_0^1xf'(x)\,dx$ (integration by parts), and $\left|\int_0^1xf'\right|\le\max|f'|\int_0^1x\,dx=\frac12\max|f'|$.

questions.prompt:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $A,B$ be two complex nonsingular $n\times n$ matrices such that
$$A^2B-2ABA+BA^2=0 .$$
Prove that the matrix $AB^{-1}A^{-1}B-I_n$ is nilpotent. (Here $I_n$ denotes the $n\times n$ identity matrix. A matrix $X$ is called nilpotent if there exists a positive integer $k$ such that $X^k=0$.)
questions.answer: The condition says $A$ commutes with $AB-BA$; from this, if $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $X=AB^{-1}A^{-1}B$ then so is $2-\frac1\lambda$. This Möbius map is $u\mapsto u+1$ in the coordinate $u=\frac1{\lambda-1}$, so a finite spectrum forces $\lambda=1$; hence $X-I$ is nilpotent.

questions.prompt:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $G$ be a simple undirected graph on $n$ vertices. Let $d_i$ be the degree of its $i$-th vertex, $i=1,\dots,n$. Denote $\Delta=\max d_i$. Prove that if
$$\sum_{i=1}^nd_i^2>n\Delta(n-\Delta)$$
then $G$ contains a triangle. (A graph is called simple if there are no loops and no multiple edges between any pair of vertices.)
questions.answer: If $G$ is triangle-free, adjacent vertices have disjoint neighbourhoods, so $d_i+d_j\le n$ on every edge and $\sum d_i^2=\sum_{ij\in E}(d_i+d_j)\le n|E|$; and $|E|\le\Delta(n-\Delta)$ because the neighbourhood of a max-degree vertex is independent.

questions.prompt:
Let $p>2$ be a prime and let
$$\mathcal A=\{n\in\mathbb N:\ 2p\mid n\ \text{and}\ p^2\nmid n\ \text{and}\ n\mid 3^n-1\}.$$
Prove that
$$\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{|\mathcal A\cap[1,k]|}{k}\le\frac{2\log3}{p\log p}.$$
questions.answer: Write $n=pr$; Fermat gives $3^n\equiv3^r\pmod p$, so $l=\operatorname{ord}_p3$ divides $r$. Thus every $n\in\mathcal A$ is a multiple of $pl$, and $3^l>p$ gives $l>\frac{\log p}{\log3}$, so the density is at most $\frac1{pl}<\frac{\log3}{p\log p}$.

questions.prompt:
Suppose that $f\colon[-1,1]\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and that
$$\left(\int_{-1}^1e^xf(x)\,dx\right)^2\ge\left(\int_{-1}^1f(x)\,dx\right)\left(\int_{-1}^1e^{2x}f(x)\,dx\right).$$
Prove that there exists a point $c\in(-1,1)$ such that $f(c)=0$.
questions.answer: If $f$ had no zero, WLOG $f>0$ on $(-1,1)$; then $t\mapsto\int(e^x-t)^2f\,dx$ is a positive quadratic, so its discriminant is negative: $\left(\int e^xf\right)^2<\int f\int e^{2x}f$ (strict Cauchy–Schwarz), a contradiction.

questions.prompt:
A real $2024\times2024$ matrix $A$ is called *nice* if $(Av,v)=1$ for every vector $v\in\mathbb R^{2024}$ with unit norm.

a) Prove that the only nice matrix such that all of its eigenvalues are real is the identity matrix.

b) Find an example of a nice non-identity matrix.
questions.answer: Nice $\iff A+A^T=2I\iff A=I+B$ with $B^T=-B$. a) $B$ has purely imaginary eigenvalues, so real eigenvalues force them to be $0$, and a normal (skew-symmetric) matrix with only zero eigenvalues is $0$. b) $A=I+E_{12}-E_{21}$.

questions.prompt:
Let $a_1>0$ and for $n\ge1$ define
$$a_{n+1}=a_n+\frac1{a_1+a_2+\dots+a_n}.$$
Prove that $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{a_n^2}{\ln n}=2$.
questions.answer: With $S_n=a_1+\dots+a_n$: $a_n\to\infty$, $\frac{S_n}{a_n}-\frac{S_{n-1}}{a_{n-1}}=1-\frac1{a_na_{n-1}}\to1$ so $\frac{S_n}{na_n}\to1$ (Cesàro), hence $n(a_{n+1}^2-a_n^2)=\frac{na_n}{S_n}\big(1+\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}\big)\to2$, and Stolz–Cesàro gives $a_n^2/\ln n\to2$.

questions.prompt:
Let $(b_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a sequence of positive integers satisfying $b_n=d\left(\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}b_k\right)$ for all $n\ge1$. (By $d(m)$ we denote the number of positive divisors of $m$.)

a) Prove that $(b_n)_{n\ge0}$ is unbounded.

b) Prove that there are infinitely many $n$ such that $b_n>b_{n+1}$.
questions.answer: With $s_n=\sum_{k<n}b_k$: $s_{n+1}=s_n+d(s_n)$. a) By CRT choose $x$ with $p_j^C\mid x+j$ ($1\le j\le C$); the walk cannot jump over $[x+1,x+C]$, giving $d(s_n)>C$. b) If $b$ were eventually nondecreasing, each value $a$ would be taken on an arithmetic progression with difference $a$ of numbers with exactly $a$ divisors; such progressions have length $<a^8$ (CRT + Mertens), while $b_n\ll n^{1/19}$ since $d(m)\ll m^{1/20}$ — too few values for too many indices.

questions.prompt: Let $a\ge2$ be an integer. Prove that there exists a positive integer $b$ with the following property: For each positive integer $n$, there is a prime number $p=p(a,b,n)$ such that $a^n+b$ is divisible by $p$ but not divisible by $p^2$.
questions.answer: If $a$ is a power of $2$, take $b=10$ (then $2\,\|\,a^n+10$, except $a=2,n=1$ where $3\,\|\,12$). Otherwise let $q$ be an odd prime factor of $a$: if $q\,\|\,a$ take $b=a$; if $q^2\mid a$ take $b=q$.

questions.prompt:
Find all real numbers $x>1$ that satisfy the equality
$$\left\lfloor\frac{n+1}{x}\right\rfloor=n-\left\lfloor\frac nx\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{\lfloor\frac nx\rfloor}{x}\right\rfloor-\left\lfloor\frac{\left\lfloor\frac{\lfloor\frac nx\rfloor}{x}\right\rfloor}{x}\right\rfloor+\dots$$
for all positive integers $n$.

Here, $\lfloor t\rfloor$ is the integer part of $t$, i.e. the integer such that $\lfloor t\rfloor\le t<\lfloor t\rfloor+1$.

Let us call a sequence $(b_1,b_2,\dots)$ of positive integers *fast-growing* if $b_{n+1}\ge b_n+2$ for all $n\ge1$. Also, for a sequence $a=(a(1),a(2),\dots)$ of real numbers and a sequence $b=(b_1,b_2,\dots)$ of positive integers, let us denote
$$S(a,b)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty\big|a(b_n)+a(b_n+1)+\dots+a(b_{n+1}-1)\big| .$$

1. Do there exist two fast-growing sequences $b=(b_1,b_2,\dots)$, $c=(c_1,c_2,\dots)$ such that for every sequence $a=(a(1),a(2),\dots)$, if all the series
$$\sum_{n=1}^\infty a(n),\qquad S(a,b)\qquad\text{and}\qquad S(a,c)$$
are convergent, then the series $\sum_{n=1}^\infty|a(n)|$ is also convergent?

2. Do there exist three fast-growing sequences $b=(b_1,b_2,\dots)$, $c=(c_1,c_2,\dots)$, $d=(d_1,d_2,\dots)$ such that for every sequence $a=(a(1),a(2),\dots)$, if all the series
$$S(a,b),\qquad S(a,c)\qquad\text{and}\qquad S(a,d)$$
are convergent, then the series $\sum_{n=1}^\infty|a(n)|$ is also convergent?

(Answer both parts, e.g. "yes, no".)
questions.answer: No, yes

questions.prompt:
Let $n\ge2$ be an integer, and let $A$ be an $n\times n$ real matrix with minimal polynomial $x^n+x-1$. Show that
$$\operatorname{tr}\big((nA^{n-1}+I)^{-1}A^{n-2}\big)=0 .$$
Here, $\operatorname{tr}(B)=\sum_{i=1}^nb_{ii}$ denotes the trace of the matrix $B=(b_{ij})_{i,j=1}^n$.
questions.answer: With $\alpha(z)=z^n+z-1$ (distinct roots $\lambda_k$, the eigenvalues of $A$) the trace is $\sum_k\frac{\lambda_k^{n-2}}{\alpha'(\lambda_k)}$, and $\sum_k\frac{g(\lambda_k)}{\alpha'(\lambda_k)}=0$ for every polynomial $g$ of degree $\le n-2$ (Lagrange interpolation).

questions.prompt: Let $x_0=a$, $x_1=b$, $x_2=c$ for given numbers $a,b,c\in\mathbb R$, and let $x_{n+2}=\dfrac{x_n+x_{n-1}}{2}$ for $n\ge1$. Show that the sequence $(x_n)_{n=0}^\infty$ converges, and find its limit.
questions.answer: $\lim x_n=\dfrac{a+2b+2c}{5}$: the differences satisfy $x_{n+4}-x_{n+3}=-\frac14(x_n-x_{n-1})$, so the sequence is Cauchy, and $x_{n+1}+x_n+\frac12x_{n-1}$ is invariant (equal to $c+b+\frac a2$).

questions.prompt: Let $A,B$ be two $n\times n$ complex matrices of the same rank, and let $k\in\mathbb N$. Prove that $A^{k+1}B^k=A$ if and only if $B^{k+1}A^k=B$.
questions.answer: From $A^{k+1}B^k=A$: $\ker B\subseteq\ker A$, so $\ker A=\ker B$, and $\operatorname{rank}A^2=\operatorname{rank}A$, so $\mathbb C^n=\operatorname{Im}A\oplus\ker A$. In such a basis $A=\begin{pmatrix}A_1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$, $B=\begin{pmatrix}B_1&0\\B_3&0\end{pmatrix}$ with $A_1^kB_1^k=I$, which gives $B^{k+1}A^k=B$; the converse is symmetric.

questions.answer: $f$ takes every value of $D$ exactly $K$ times ($K$ = number of zeros, by Rouché), so the area of $f(D)$ with multiplicity, $\iint_D|f'|^2=\pi\sum n|a_n|^2$, equals $K\pi$. (Alternatively: $f$ is a finite Blaschke product and $\sum n|a_n|^2=\frac1{2\pi i}\oint\frac{f'}{f}dz=K$.)

questions.prompt:
Let $n$ be an odd integer and let $A$ and $B$ be complex $n\times n$ matrices such that $A$, $B$, $A-B$ are invertible and
$$(A-B)^{-1}=A^{-1}-B^{-1}.$$
Prove that
$$\det A\,\det B=-\big(\det(A-B)\big)^2 .$$
questions.answer: With $X=AB^{-1}$ the hypothesis gives $X^2-X+I=0$, hence $X^3=-I$ and $X-I=-X^{-1}$; so $(\det X)^3=-1$ and $\det(A-B)^2=\det B^2/\det(X)^2$, which yields the identity ($n$ odd is used twice).

Let $f\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be a bounded continuous function. Suppose that there exists a positive number $a$ such that
$$g(x)=f(x)+a\int_{x-1}^{x}f(t)\,dt,\qquad x\in\mathbb R,$$
is a constant function. Show that $f$ is a constant function.
questions.answer: For $u=f-\frac{C}{1+a}$ the functional $V(x)=\frac12u(x)^2+\frac a2\int_{x-1}^xu^2$ satisfies $V'=-\frac a2\big(u(x)-u(x-1)\big)^2\le0$; a compactness (translation-limit) argument shows $V(\pm\infty)=0$, so $V\equiv0$ and $f\equiv\frac C{1+a}$.

$$x+y^n\ \text{ is divisible by }\ z=\frac{(x+y)^n-y^n}{x}-1 .$$
